197|def parse_sources(config: Any, *, root_field: str = DEFAULT_ROOT_FIELD) -> dict[str, Source]:
198|    """
199|    Parse an entire sources table like `[tool.hatch.envs.default.sources]`. Returns a mapping keyed by
200|    [normalized](https://peps.python.org/pep-0503/#normalized-names) project name.
201|    `root_field` is the location of the table being parsed, used in error messages.
202|    """
203|    from collections import defaultdict
204|
205|    from hatch.utils.metadata import normalize_project_name
206|
207|    if not isinstance(config, dict):
208|        message = f"Field `{root_field}` must be a table"
209|        raise TypeError(message)
210|
211|    sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
212|    original_names: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
213|
214|    for name, raw in config.items():
215|        if not isinstance(name, str):
216|            message = f"Source names in `{root_field}` must be strings"
217|            raise TypeError(message)
218|
219|        if not name:
220|            message = f"Source names in `{root_field}` cannot be empty"
221|            raise ValueError(message)
222|
223|        normalized = normalize_project_name(name)
224|        original_names[normalized].append(name)
225|        sources[normalized] = parse_source(name, raw, root_field=root_field)
226|
227|    duplicates = [
228|        f"{normed} ({', '.join(originals)})" for normed, originals in original_names.items() if len(originals) > 1
229|    ]
230|    if duplicates:
231|        message = f"Field `{root_field}` contains duplicate names: {', '.join(duplicates)}"
232|        raise ValueError(message)

308|def apply_source_to_requirement(
309|    name: str,
310|    extras: list[str],
311|    source: Source,
312|    root: str,
313|    workspace_members: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
314|) -> tuple[str, bool] | None:
315|    """
316|    Rewrite a requirement so it points at the given source. Returns a tuple of
317|    `(requirement_string, editable)` suitable for constructing a new `Dependency`,
318|    or `None` if the source does not rewrite the requirement (e.g. `IndexSource`,
319|    or a `WorkspaceSource` that cannot be matched to a member in `workspace_members`).
320|
321|    `workspace_members` maps [normalized](https://peps.python.org/pep-0503/#normalized-names)
322|    project names to the local path of the matching workspace member.
323|    """
324|    extras_segment = f"[{','.join(extras)}]" if extras else ""
325|
326|    if isinstance(source, PathSource):
327|        if source.editable and source.subdirectory:
328|            # Editable installs pass a bare directory to the installer, where a
329|            # `#subdirectory` fragment would be treated as part of the filesystem
330|            # path, so resolve the subdirectory into the path itself.
331|            import os
332|
333|            url = render_path_url(os.path.join(source.path, source.subdirectory), root)
334|            return f"{name}{extras_segment} @ {url}", True
335|
336|        url = render_path_url(source.path, root, subdirectory=source.subdirectory)
337|        return f"{name}{extras_segment} @ {url}", source.editable
338|
339|    if isinstance(source, GitSource):
340|        url = render_git_url(source)
341|        return f"{name}{extras_segment} @ {url}", False
342|
343|    if isinstance(source, UrlSource):
344|        url = render_url(source)
345|        return f"{name}{extras_segment} @ {url}", False
346|
347|    if isinstance(source, WorkspaceSource):
348|        if workspace_members is None:
349|            return None
350|
351|        from hatch.utils.metadata import normalize_project_name
352|
353|        member_path = workspace_members.get(normalize_project_name(name))
354|        if member_path is None:
355|            return None
356|
357|        # Workspace members are installed editable, matching `local_dependencies_complex`.
358|        url = render_path_url(member_path, root)
359|        return f"{name}{extras_segment} @ {url}", True
360|
361|    return None

364|def collect_global_install_args(dependencies: Iterable[Dependency], sources: Mapping[str, Source]) -> list[str]:
365|    """
366|    Collect installer flags that apply to the entire install command (rather
367|    than to a single dependency). Currently this surfaces every `IndexSource`
368|    matching one of the given dependencies as `--extra-index-url`, deduplicated
369|    and order-preserving so PyPI remains the primary index.
370|    """
371|    args: list[str] = []
372|    seen: set[str] = set()
373|    for dependency in dependencies:
374|        # An explicit direct reference always wins over a configured source
375|        if dependency.url is not None:
376|            continue
377|
378|        source = lookup(sources, dependency.name)
379|        if isinstance(source, IndexSource) and source.index not in seen:
380|            seen.add(source.index)
381|            args.extend(["--extra-index-url", source.index])
382|
383|    return args

386|def decorate_dependency(
387|    dependency: Dependency,
388|    sources: Mapping[str, Source],
389|    root: str,
390|    workspace_members: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
391|) -> Dependency:
392|    """
393|    Apply a matching source from `sources` to `dependency`, returning a new
394|    [`Dependency`](../utilities.md#hatch.dep.core.Dependency) if a rewrite is
395|    needed, or the original dependency otherwise.
396|
397|    Dependencies that already define a PEP 508 direct reference are left alone.
398|
399|    `workspace_members` maps [normalized](https://peps.python.org/pep-0503/#normalized-names)
400|    project names to the local path of the matching workspace member, used to resolve
401|    [`WorkspaceSource`](#WorkspaceSource) entries.
402|    """
403|    from hatch.dep.core import Dependency
404|
405|    if dependency.url is not None:
406|        return dependency
407|
408|    source = lookup(sources, dependency.name)
409|    if source is None:
410|        return dependency
411|
412|    rewritten = apply_source_to_requirement(dependency.name, list(dependency.extras), source, root, workspace_members)
413|    if rewritten is None:
414|        if isinstance(source, WorkspaceSource):
415|            # A `WorkspaceSource` that reaches here could not be matched to a member, which
416|            # is a configuration error. Installing from a default index would silently ignore
417|            # the declared source, so fail loudly instead.
418|            message = (
419|                f"Dependency `{dependency.name}` declares `workspace = true` in its environment's "
420|                f"`sources` but no matching member was found in `tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>.workspace.members`"
421|            )
422|            raise ValueError(message)
423|
424|        # `IndexSource` becomes an install-wide flag rather than changing the requirement
425|        return dependency
426|
427|    spec, editable = rewritten
428|    if dependency.marker is not None:
429|        spec = f"{spec} ; {dependency.marker}"
430|
431|    return Dependency(spec, editable=editable)

434|def decorate_dependencies(

437|    root: str,

439|) -> list[Dependency]:

449|def source_applied(

451|) -> bool:
452|    """

39|class BorrowedStatus(TerminalStatus):
40|    def __init__(
41|        self,
42|        console: Console,
43|        *,
44|        is_interactive: bool,
45|        verbosity: int,
46|        spinner_style: str,
47|        waiting_style: Style | str,
48|        success_style: Style | str,

50|        finalizer: Callable,
51|    ):
52|        self.__console = console
53|        self.__is_interactive = is_interactive
54|        self.__verbosity = verbosity
55|        self.__spinner_style = spinner_style
56|        self.__waiting_style = waiting_style
57|        self.__success_style = success_style
58|        self.__initializer = initializer
59|        self.__finalizer = finalizer
60|
61|        # This is the possibly active current status
62|        self.__status: Status | None = None
63|
64|        # This is used as a stack to display the current message
65|        self.__messages: list[tuple[Text, str]] = []
66|
67|    def stop(self) -> None:
68|        active = self.__active()
69|        if self.__status is not None:
70|            self.__status.stop()
71|            self.__finalizer()
72|
73|        old_message, final_text = self.__messages[-1]
74|        if self.__verbosity > 0 and active:
75|            if not final_text:
76|                final_text = old_message.plain
77|                final_text = f"Finished {final_text[:1].lower()}{final_text[1:]}"
78|
79|            self.__output(Text(final_text, style=self.__success_style))

82|        self.__messages.append((Text(message, style=self.__waiting_style), final_text))

107|            if not final_text:

1|"""
2|Resolve and write environment lockfiles (PEP 751 ``pylock.toml``) via pluggable **lockers**.
3|
4|Lockers are registered with ``hatch_register_locker``; built-ins ``uv`` and ``pip`` delegate to
5|``uv pip compile`` / ``pip lock``. See ``docs/how-to/environment/lockfiles.md``.
6|"""
7|
8|from __future__ import annotations
9|
10|from dataclasses import dataclass
11|from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
12|
13|if TYPE_CHECKING:
14|    from collections.abc import Callable
15|
16|    from hatch.env.lockers.interface import LockerInterface
17|    from hatch.env.plugin.interface import EnvironmentInterface
18|    from hatch.project.core import Project
19|    from hatch.utils.fs import Path
20|
21|
22|class LockerNotFoundError(Exception):
23|    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
24|        super().__init__(f"Unknown locker plugin: {name}")
25|        self.name = name
26|
27|
28|class LockerUnsupportedError(Exception):
29|    def __init__(self, name: str, *, detail: str = "") -> None:
30|        msg = f"Locker `{name}` does not support this environment"
31|        if detail:
32|            msg = f"{msg}: {detail}"
33|        super().__init__(msg)
34|        self.name = name
35|        self.detail = detail
36|
37|
38|@dataclass
39|class LockGenerationState:
40|    """Inputs for :meth:`LockerInterface.generate` / :meth:`LockerInterface.in_sync`."""
41|
42|    dependencies: list[str]
43|    layered: bool
44|    lock_extras: tuple[str, ...]
45|    lock_groups: tuple[str, ...]
46|
47|
48|def environment_has_lock_inputs(environment: EnvironmentInterface) -> bool:
49|    """Whether the environment has anything to pass to the lock resolver."""
50|    if environment.environment_dependencies or environment.additional_dependencies:
51|        return True
52|    if environment.features or environment.dependency_groups:
53|        return (environment.root / "pyproject.toml").is_file()
54|    if not environment.skip_install and (environment.root / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
55|        return True
56|    return bool(environment.dependencies)
57|
58|
59|def _lock_environment_only_strings(environment: EnvironmentInterface) -> list[str]:
60|    lines = list(environment.environment_dependencies)
61|    lines.extend(map(str, environment.additional_dependencies))
62|    return lines
63|
64|
65|def _uv_should_use_layered_lock(
66|    environment: EnvironmentInterface,
67|    lock_extras: tuple[str, ...],
68|    lock_groups: tuple[str, ...],
69|) -> bool:
70|    if not (environment.root / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
71|        return False
72|    if lock_extras or lock_groups:
73|        return True
74|    return not environment.skip_install
75|
76|
77|def prepare_lock_generation_state(
78|    environment: EnvironmentInterface,
79|    *,
80|    deps_override: list[str] | None = None,
81|    lock_extras: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
82|    lock_groups: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
83|) -> LockGenerationState | None:
84|    """
85|    Compute PEP 508 dependency lines and layered flags for the active locker.
86|
87|    Returns ``None`` when there is nothing to lock (same conditions as skipping generation).
88|    """
89|    from hatch.env.virtual import VirtualEnvironment
90|
91|    extras = lock_extras if lock_extras is not None else tuple(environment.features)
92|    groups = lock_groups if lock_groups is not None else tuple(environment.dependency_groups)
93|
94|    uv = isinstance(environment, VirtualEnvironment) and environment.use_uv
95|    layered = uv and _uv_should_use_layered_lock(environment, extras, groups)
96|
97|    if layered:
98|        direct_deps = deps_override if deps_override is not None else _lock_environment_only_strings(environment)
99|    else:
100|        direct_deps = deps_override if deps_override is not None else list(environment.dependencies)
101|        extras = ()
102|        groups = ()
103|
104|    pyproject = environment.root / "pyproject.toml"
105|    if layered and not direct_deps and not pyproject.is_file():
106|        return None
107|
108|    if not direct_deps and not (layered and pyproject.is_file()):
109|        return None
110|
111|    return LockGenerationState(
112|        dependencies=list(direct_deps),
113|        layered=layered,
114|        lock_extras=extras,
115|        lock_groups=groups,
116|    )
117|
118|
119|def get_locker_plugin_class(project: Project, environment: EnvironmentInterface) -> type[LockerInterface]:
120|    name: str | None = environment.config.get("locker")
121|    if name is None:
122|        name = project.config.locker
123|    if name is None:
124|        from hatch.env.virtual import VirtualEnvironment
125|
126|        name = "uv" if isinstance(environment, VirtualEnvironment) and environment.use_uv else "pip"
127|
128|    cls = project.plugin_manager.locker.get(name)
129|    if cls is None:
130|        raise LockerNotFoundError(name)
131|    if not cls.supports(environment):
132|        raise LockerUnsupportedError(name)
133|
134|    return cls
135|
136|
137|def generate_lockfile(
138|    environment: EnvironmentInterface,
139|    output_path: Path,
140|    *,
141|    upgrade: bool = False,
142|    upgrade_packages: tuple[str, ...] = (),
143|    deps_override: list[str] | None = None,
144|    lock_extras: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
145|    lock_groups: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
146|) -> None:
147|    state = prepare_lock_generation_state(
148|        environment,
149|        deps_override=deps_override,
150|        lock_extras=lock_extras,
151|        lock_groups=lock_groups,
152|    )
153|    if state is None:
154|        return
155|
156|    locker_cls = get_locker_plugin_class(environment.app.project, environment)
157|    locker_cls.generate(
158|        environment,
159|        state.dependencies,
160|        output_path,
161|        upgrade=upgrade,
162|        upgrade_packages=upgrade_packages,
163|        layered=state.layered,
164|        lock_extras=state.lock_extras,
165|        lock_groups=state.lock_groups,
166|    )
167|
168|
169|def lockfile_in_sync(
170|    environment: EnvironmentInterface,
171|    output_path: Path,
172|    *,
173|    upgrade: bool = False,
174|    upgrade_packages: tuple[str, ...] = (),
175|    deps_override: list[str] | None = None,
176|    lock_extras: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
177|    lock_groups: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
178|) -> bool:
179|    """Whether ``output_path`` matches a fresh resolution (see :meth:`LockerInterface.in_sync`)."""
180|    state = prepare_lock_generation_state(
181|        environment,
182|        deps_override=deps_override,
183|        lock_extras=lock_extras,
184|        lock_groups=lock_groups,
185|    )
186|    if state is None:
187|        return output_path.is_file()
188|
189|    locker_cls = get_locker_plugin_class(environment.app.project, environment)
190|    return locker_cls.in_sync(
191|        environment,
192|        state.dependencies,
193|        output_path,
194|        upgrade=upgrade,
195|        upgrade_packages=upgrade_packages,
196|        layered=state.layered,
197|        lock_extras=state.lock_extras,
198|        lock_groups=state.lock_groups,
199|    )
200|
201|
202|verify_lockfile = lockfile_in_sync
203|
204|
205|def apply_lock_with_locker(environment: EnvironmentInterface, lock_path: Path) -> None:
206|    """Apply the lockfile at ``lock_path`` using the configured locker."""
207|    locker_cls = get_locker_plugin_class(environment.app.project, environment)
208|    locker_cls.apply_lock(environment, lock_path)
209|
210|
211|def apply_lockfile_to_environment(environment: EnvironmentInterface, lock_path: Path | None = None) -> None:
212|    """Same as :func:`apply_lock_with_locker` using ``lock_path`` or :func:`resolve_lockfile_path`."""
213|    path = resolve_lockfile_path(environment) if lock_path is None else lock_path
214|    apply_lock_with_locker(environment, path)

216|
217|def merge_environment_lock_inputs(
218|    project: Project,
219|    env_names: list[str],
220|    abort: Callable[[str], None],
221|) -> tuple[EnvironmentInterface, list[str] | None, tuple[str, ...] | None, tuple[str, ...] | None, str]:
222|    """
223|    Merge dependency lines for environments that share one lockfile (matrix / ``lock-filename``).
224|
225|    Returns ``(representative_environment, deps_override, lock_extras, lock_groups, display_label)``.
226|    Overrides are ``None`` when only a single environment is involved (use the env's own config).
227|    """
228|    from hatch.env.virtual import VirtualEnvironment
229|
230|    if len(env_names) == 1:
231|        environment = project.get_environment(env_names[0])
232|        return environment, None, None, None, env_names[0]
233|
234|    seen_full: set[str] = set()
235|    merged_full: list[str] = []
236|    seen_env_only: set[str] = set()
237|    merged_env_only: list[str] = []
238|    python_versions: set[str] = set()
239|    extras_union: set[str] = set()
240|    groups_union: set[str] = set()
241|    for env in env_names:
242|        env_obj = project.get_environment(env)
243|        for dep in env_obj.dependencies:
244|            if dep not in seen_full:
245|                seen_full.add(dep)
246|                merged_full.append(dep)
247|        for dep in env_obj.environment_dependencies:
248|            if dep not in seen_env_only:
249|                seen_env_only.add(dep)
250|                merged_env_only.append(dep)
251|        for dep in env_obj.additional_dependencies:
252|            dep_s = str(dep)
253|            if dep_s not in seen_env_only:
254|                seen_env_only.add(dep_s)
255|                merged_env_only.append(dep_s)
256|        extras_union.update(env_obj.features)
257|        groups_union.update(env_obj.dependency_groups)
258|        python_version = env_obj.config.get("python", "")
259|        python_versions.add(python_version)
260|
261|    if len(python_versions) > 1:
262|        versions_str = ", ".join(sorted(v for v in python_versions if v) or ["(default)"])
263|        abort(
264|            f"Environments sharing this lockfile target different Python versions ({versions_str}). "
265|            f"A single lockfile cannot be valid across different Python versions. "
266|            f"Use distinct `lock-filename` values for each Python version."
267|        )
268|
269|    environment = project.get_environment(env_names[0])
270|    display_name = ", ".join(env_names)
271|    use_layered_merge = (
272|        isinstance(environment, VirtualEnvironment)
273|        and environment.use_uv
274|        and (environment.root / "pyproject.toml").is_file()
275|        and (extras_union or groups_union or any(not project.get_environment(e).skip_install for e in env_names))
276|    )
277|    if use_layered_merge:
278|        merged_deps = merged_env_only
279|        merged_extras = tuple(sorted(extras_union))
280|        merged_groups = tuple(sorted(groups_union))
281|    else:
282|        merged_deps = merged_full
283|        merged_extras = ()
284|        merged_groups = ()
285|
286|    return environment, merged_deps, merged_extras, merged_groups, display_name
287|
288|
289|def resolve_lockfile_path(environment: EnvironmentInterface) -> Path:
290|    lock_filename = environment.config.get("lock-filename")
291|    if lock_filename:
292|        # Format the configured filename using the project's context with the
293|        # environment-specific formatters applied so context fields like
294|        # {env_name}, {matrix:...}, etc. are resolved.
295|        with environment.metadata.context.apply_context(environment.context):
296|            lock_filename = environment.metadata.context.format(lock_filename)
297|        return environment.root / lock_filename
298|
299|    if environment.name == "default":
300|        return environment.root / "pylock.toml"
301|
302|    # PEP 751 only allows one dot in the filename: pylock.<name>.toml
303|    safe_name = environment.name.replace(".", "-")
304|    return environment.root / f"pylock.{safe_name}.toml"

1|# Build configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|[Build targets](#build-targets) are defined as sections within `tool.hatch.build.targets`:
6|
7|```toml config-example
8|[tool.hatch.build.targets.<TARGET_NAME>]
9|```
10|
11|!!! tip
12|    Although not recommended, you may define global configuration in the `tool.hatch.build` table. Keys may then be overridden by target config.
13|
14|## Build system
15|
16|To be compatible with the broader [Python packaging ecosystem](../build.md#packaging-ecosystem), you must define the [build system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/#source-trees) as follows:
17|
18|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
19|[build-system]
20|requires = ["hatchling"]
21|build-backend = "hatchling.build"
22|```
23|
24|The version of `hatchling` defined here will be used to build all targets.
25|
26|Hatchling is a standards-compliant[^1] build backend and is a dependency of Hatch itself.
27|
28|## File selection
29|
30|### VCS
31|
32|By default, Hatch will respect the first `.gitignore` or `.hgignore` file found in your project's root directory or parent directories. Set `ignore-vcs` to `true` to disable this behavior:
33|
34|```toml config-example
35|[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
36|ignore-vcs = true
37|```
38|
39|!!! note
40|    For `.hgignore` files only glob syntax is supported.
41|
42|### Patterns
43|
44|You can set the `include` and `exclude` options to select exactly which files will be shipped in each build, with `exclude` taking precedence. Every entry represents a [Git-style glob pattern](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore#_pattern_format).
45|
46|For example, the following configuration:
47|
48|```toml config-example
49|[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
50|include = [
51|  "pkg/*.py",
52|  "/tests",
53|]
54|exclude = [
55|  "*.json",
56|  "pkg/_compat.py",
57|]
58|```
59|
60|will exclude every file with a `.json` extension, and will include everything under a `tests` directory located at the root and every file with a `.py` extension that is directly under a `pkg` directory located at the root except for `_compat.py`.
61|
62|### Artifacts
63|
64|If you want to include files that are [ignored by your VCS](#vcs), such as those that might be created by [build hooks](#build-hooks), you can use the `artifacts` option. This option is semantically equivalent to `include`.
65|
66|Note that artifacts are not affected by the `exclude` option. Artifacts can
67|be excluded by using more explicit paths or by using the `!` negation operator.
68|When using the `!` operator, the negated pattern(s) must come after the more
69|generic ones.
70|
71|```toml config-example
72|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
73|artifacts = [
74|  "*.so",
75|  "*.dll",
76|  "!/foo/*.so",
77|]
78|```
79|
80|### Explicit selection
81|
82|#### Generic
83|
84|You can use the `only-include` option to prevent directory traversal starting at the project root and only select specific relative paths to directories or files. Using this option ignores any defined [`include` patterns](#patterns).
85|
86|```toml config-example
87|[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
88|only-include = ["pkg", "tests/unit"]
89|```
90|
91|#### Packages
92|
93|The `packages` option is semantically equivalent to `only-include` (which takes precedence) except that the shipped path will be collapsed to only include the final component.
94|
95|So for example, if you want to ship a package `foo` that is stored in a directory `src` you would do:
96|
97|```toml config-example
98|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
99|packages = ["src/foo"]
100|```
101|
102|### Forced inclusion
103|
104|The `force-include` option allows you to select specific files or directories from anywhere on the file system that should be included and map them to the desired relative distribution path.
105|
106|For example, if there was a directory alongside the project root named `artifacts` containing a file named `lib.so` and a file named `lib.h` in your home directory, you could ship both files in a `pkg` directory with the following configuration:
107|
108|```toml config-example
109|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
110|"../artifacts" = "pkg"
111|"~/lib.h" = "pkg/lib.h"
112|```
113|
114|!!! note
115|    - Files must be mapped exactly to their desired paths, not to directories.
116|    - The contents of directory sources are recursively included.
117|    - To map directory contents directly to the root use `/` (a forward slash).
118|    - Sources that do not exist will raise an error.
119|
120|!!! warning
121|    Attempting to overwrite any file path that was already included by other file selection options will raise an error.
122|
123|### Default file selection
124|
125|If no file selection options are provided, then what gets included is determined by each [build target](#build-targets).
126|
127|### Excluding files outside packages
128|
129|If you want to exclude non-[artifact](#artifacts) files that do not reside within a Python package, set `only-packages` to `true`:
130|
131|```toml config-example
132|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
133|only-packages = true
134|```
135|
136|### Rewriting paths
137|
138|You can rewrite relative paths to directories with the `sources` option. For example, the following configuration:
139|
140|```toml config-example
141|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.sources]
142|"src/foo" = "bar"
143|```
144|
145|would distribute the file `src/foo/file.ext` as `bar/file.ext`.
146|
147|If you want to remove path prefixes entirely, rather than setting each to an empty string, you can define `sources` as an array:
148|
149|```toml config-example
150|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
151|sources = ["src"]
152|```
153|
154|If you want to add a prefix to paths, you can use an empty string. For example, the following configuration:
155|
156|```toml config-example
157|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.sources]
158|"" = "foo"
159|```
160|
161|would distribute the file `bar/file.ext` as `foo/bar/file.ext`.
162|
163|The [packages](#packages) option itself relies on sources. Defining `#!toml packages = ["src/foo"]` for the `wheel` target is equivalent to the following:
164|
165|```toml config-example
166|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
167|only-include = ["src/foo"]
168|sources = ["src"]
169|```
170|
171|### Performance
172|
173|All encountered directories are traversed by default. To skip non-[artifact](#artifacts) directories that are excluded, set `skip-excluded-dirs` to `true`:
174|
175|```toml config-example
176|[tool.hatch.build]
177|skip-excluded-dirs = true
178|```
179|
180|!!! warning
181|    This may result in not shipping desired files. For example, if you want to include the file `a/b/c.txt` but your [VCS ignores](#vcs) `a/b`, the file `c.txt` will not be seen because its parent directory will not be entered. In such cases you can use the [`force-include`](#forced-inclusion) option.
182|
183|## Reproducible builds
184|
185|By default, [build targets](#build-targets) will build in a reproducible manner provided that they support that behavior. To disable this, set `reproducible` to `false`:
186|
187|```toml config-example
188|[tool.hatch.build]
189|reproducible = false
190|```
191|
192|When enabled, the [SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH](https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/) environment variable will be used for all build timestamps. If not set, then Hatch will use an [unchanging default value](../plugins/utilities.md#hatchling.builders.utils.get_reproducible_timestamp).
193|
194|## Output directory
195|
196|When the output directory is not provided to the [`build`](../cli/reference.md#hatch-build) command, the `dist` directory will be used by default. You can change the default to a different directory using a relative or absolute path like so:
197|
198|```toml config-example
199|[tool.hatch.build]
200|directory = "<PATH>"
201|```
202|
203|## Dev mode
204|
205|By default for [dev mode](environment/overview.md#dev-mode) environment installations or [editable installs](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/local-project-installs/#editable-installs), the `wheel` target will determine which directories should be added to Python's search path based on the [selected files](#file-selection).
206|
207|If you want to override this detection or perhaps instruct other build targets as well, you can use the `dev-mode-dirs` option:
208|
209|```toml config-example
210|[tool.hatch.build]
211|dev-mode-dirs = ["."]
212|```
213|
214|If you don't want to add entire directories to Python's search path, you can enable a more targeted mechanism with the mutually exclusive `dev-mode-exact` option:
215|
216|```toml config-example
217|[tool.hatch.build]
218|dev-mode-exact = true
219|```
220|
221|!!! warning
222|    The `dev-mode-exact` mechanism is [not supported](https://github.com/microsoft/pylance-release/issues/2114) by static analysis tools & IDEs, therefore functionality such as autocompletion is unlikely to work.
223|
224|## Build targets
225|
226|A build target can be provided by any [builder plugin](../plugins/builder/reference.md). There are three built-in build targets: [wheel](../plugins/builder/wheel.md), [sdist](../plugins/builder/sdist.md), and [custom](../plugins/builder/custom.md).
227|
228|### Dependencies ### {: #target-dependencies }
229|
230|You can specify additional dependencies that will be installed in each build environment, such as for third party builders:
231|
232|```toml config-example
233|[tool.hatch.build.targets.your-target-name]
234|dependencies = [
235|  "your-builder-plugin"
236|]
237|```
238|
239|You can also declare dependence on the project's [runtime dependencies](metadata.md#required) with the `require-runtime-dependencies` option:
240|
241|```toml config-example
242|[tool.hatch.build.targets.your-target-name]
243|require-runtime-dependencies = true
244|```
245|
246|Additionally, you may declare dependence on specific [runtime features](metadata.md#optional) of the project with the `require-runtime-features` option:
247|
248|```toml config-example
249|[tool.hatch.build.targets.your-target-name]
250|require-runtime-features = [
251|  "feature1",
252|  "feature2",
253|]
254|```
255|
256|### Versions
257|
258|If a build target supports multiple build strategies or if there are major changes over time, you can specify exactly which versions you want to build using the `versions` option:
259|
260|```toml config-example
261|[tool.hatch.build.targets.<TARGET_NAME>]
262|versions = [
263|  "v1",
264|  "beta-feature",
265|]
266|```
267|
268|See the [wheel](../plugins/builder/wheel.md#versions) target for a real world example.
269|
270|## Build hooks
271|
272|A build hook defines code that will be executed at various stages of the build process and can be provided by any [build hook plugin](../plugins/build-hook/reference.md). There is one built-in build hook: [custom](../plugins/build-hook/custom.md).
273|
274|Build hooks can be applied either globally:
275|
276|```toml config-example
277|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.<HOOK_NAME>]
278|```
279|
280|or to specific build targets:
281|
282|```toml config-example
283|[tool.hatch.build.targets.<TARGET_NAME>.hooks.<HOOK_NAME>]
284|```
285|
286|### Dependencies ### {: #hook-dependencies }
287|
288|You can specify additional dependencies that will be installed in each build environment, such as for third party build hooks:
289|
290|```toml config-example
291|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.your-hook-name]
292|dependencies = [
293|  "your-build-hook-plugin"
294|]
295|```
296|
297|You can also declare dependence on the project's [runtime dependencies](metadata.md#required) with the `require-runtime-dependencies` option:
298|
299|```toml config-example
300|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.your-hook-name]
301|require-runtime-dependencies = true
302|```
303|
304|Additionally, you may declare dependence on specific [runtime features](metadata.md#optional) of the project with the `require-runtime-features` option:
305|
306|```toml config-example
307|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.your-hook-name]
308|require-runtime-features = [
309|  "feature1",
310|  "feature2",
311|]
312|```
313|
314|### Order of execution
315|
316|For each build target, build hooks execute in the order in which they are defined, starting with global hooks.
317|
318|As an example, for the following configuration:
319|
320|```toml config-example
321|[tool.hatch.build.targets.foo.hooks.hook2]
322|
323|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.hook3]
324|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.hook1]
325|```
326|
327|When target `foo` is built, build hook `hook3` will be executed first, followed by `hook1`, and then finally `hook2`.
328|
329|### Conditional execution
330|
331|If you want to disable a build hook by default and control its use by [environment variables](#environment-variables), you can do so by setting the `enable-by-default` option to `false`:
332|
333|```toml config-example
334|[tool.hatch.build.hooks.<HOOK_NAME>]
335|enable-by-default = false
336|```
337|
338|## Environment variables
339|
340|| Variable | Default | Description |
341|| --- | --- | --- |
342|| `HATCH_BUILD_CLEAN` | `false` | Whether or not existing artifacts should first be removed |
343|| `HATCH_BUILD_CLEAN_HOOKS_AFTER` | `false` | Whether or not build hook artifacts should be removed after each build |
344|| `HATCH_BUILD_HOOKS_ONLY` | `false` | Whether or not to only execute build hooks |
345|| `HATCH_BUILD_NO_HOOKS` | `false` | Whether or not to disable all build hooks; this takes precedence over other options |
346|| `HATCH_BUILD_HOOKS_ENABLE` | `false` | Whether or not to enable all build hooks |
347|| `HATCH_BUILD_HOOK_ENABLE_<HOOK_NAME>` | `false` | Whether or not to enable the build hook named `<HOOK_NAME>` |
348|| `HATCH_BUILD_LOCATION` | `dist` | The location with which to build the targets; only used by the [`build`](../cli/reference.md#hatch-build) command |
349|
350|[^1]: Support for [PEP 517][] and [PEP 660][] guarantees interoperability with other build tools.

238|def _guess_linux_variant_cpu() -> str:
239|    # Use the highest that we know is most common when we can't parse CPU data
240|    default = "v3"
241|    try:
242|        # Don't use our utility Path so we can properly mock
243|        with open("/proc/cpuinfo", encoding="utf-8") as f:
244|            contents = f.read()
245|    except OSError:
246|        return default
247|
248|    # See https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#x86 for the
249|    # instructions for each architecture variant and
250|    # https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/arch/x86/include/asm/cpufeatures.h
251|    # for the corresponding Linux flags
252|    v2_flags = {"cx16", "lahf_lm", "popcnt", "pni", "sse4_1", "sse4_2", "ssse3"}
253|    v3_flags = {"avx", "avx2", "bmi1", "bmi2", "f16c", "fma", "movbe", "xsave"} | v2_flags
254|    v4_flags = {"avx512f", "avx512bw", "avx512cd", "avx512dq", "avx512vl"} | v3_flags
255|
256|    for line in contents.splitlines():
257|        key, _, value = line.partition(":")
258|        if key.strip() == "flags":
259|            flags = set(value.strip().split())
260|
261|            if flags.issuperset(v4_flags):
262|                return "v4"
263|
264|            if flags.issuperset(v3_flags):
265|                return "v3"
266|
267|            if flags.issuperset(v2_flags):
268|                return "v2"
269|
270|            return "v1"
271|
272|    return default

1|# Dependency configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|[Project dependencies](metadata.md#dependencies) are defined with [PEP 508][] strings using optional [PEP 440 version specifiers][].
6|
7|## Version specifiers
8|
9|A version specifier consists of a series of version clauses, separated by commas. For example:
10|
11|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
12|[project]
13|...
14|dependencies = [
15|  "cryptography",
16|  "click>=7, <9, != 8.0.0",
17|  "python-dateutil==2.8.*",
18|  "numpy~=1.21.4",
19|]
20|```
21|
22|The comma is equivalent to a logical `AND` operator: a candidate version must match all given version clauses in order to match the specifier as a whole.
23|
24|### Operators
25|
26|| Operators | Function |
27|| :---: | --- |
28|| `~=` | [Compatible release](#compatible-release) |
29|| `==` | [Version matching](#version-matching) |
30|| `!=` | [Version exclusion](#version-exclusion) |
31|| `<=`, `>=` | [Inclusive ordered comparison](#ordered-comparison) |
32|| `<`, `>` | [Exclusive ordered comparison](#ordered-comparison) |
33|| `===` | [Arbitrary equality](#arbitrary-equality) |
34|
35|### Version matching
36|
37|A version matching clause includes the version matching operator `==` and a version identifier.
38|
39|By default, the version matching operator is based on a strict equality comparison: the specified version must be exactly the same as the requested version.
40|
41|| Clause | Allowed versions |
42|| --- | --- |
43|| `==1` | `1.0.0` |
44|| `==1.2` | `1.2.0` |
45|
46|Prefix matching may be requested instead of strict comparison, by appending a trailing `.*` to the version identifier in the version matching clause. This means that additional trailing segments will be ignored when determining whether or not a version identifier matches the clause.
47|
48|| Clause | Allowed versions |
49|| --- | --- |
50|| `==1.*` | `>=1.0.0, <2.0.0` |
51|| `==1.2.*` | `>=1.2.0, <1.3.0` |
52|
53|### Compatible release
54|
55|A compatible release clause consists of the compatible release operator `~=` and a version identifier. It matches any candidate version that is expected to be compatible with the specified version.
56|
57|For a given release identifier `V.N`, the compatible release clause is approximately equivalent to the following pair of comparison clauses:
58|
59|```
60|>= V.N, == V.*
61|```
62|
63|This operator cannot be used with a single segment version number such as `~=1`.
64|
65|| Clause | Allowed versions |
66|| --- | --- |
67|| `~=1.2` | `>=1.2.0, <2.0.0` |
68|| `~=1.2.3` | `>=1.2.3, <1.3.0` |
69|
70|### Version exclusion
71|
72|A version exclusion clause includes the version exclusion operator `!=` and a version identifier.
73|
74|The allowed version identifiers and comparison semantics are the same as those of the [Version matching](#version-matching) operator, except that the sense of any match is inverted.
75|
76|### Ordered comparison
77|
78|Inclusive comparisons allow for the version identifier part of clauses whereas exclusive comparisons do not. For example, `>=1.2` allows for version `1.2.0` while `>1.2` does not.
79|
80|Unlike the inclusive ordered comparisons `<=` and `>=`, the exclusive ordered comparisons `<` and `>` specifically exclude pre-releases, post-releases, and local versions of the specified version.
81|
82|### Arbitrary equality
83|
84|Though heavily discouraged, arbitrary equality comparisons allow for simple string matching without any version semantics, for example `===foobar`.
85|
86|## Environment markers
87|
88|[Environment markers](https://peps.python.org/pep-0508/#environment-markers) allow for dependencies to only be installed when certain conditions are met.
89|
90|For example, if you need to install the latest version of `cryptography` that is available for a given Python major version you could define the following:
91|
92|```
93|cryptography==3.3.2; python_version < "3"
94|cryptography>=35.0; python_version > "3"
95|```
96|
97|Alternatively, if you only need it on Python 3 when running on Windows you could do:
98|
99|```
100|cryptography; python_version ~= "3.0" and platform_system == "Windows"
101|```
102|
103|The available environment markers are as follows.
104|
105|| Marker | Python equivalent | Examples |
106|| --- | --- | --- |
107|| `os_name` | `#!python import os`<br>`os.name` | <ul><li>posix</li><li>java</li></ul> |
108|| `sys_platform` | `#!python import sys`<br>`sys.platform` | <ul><li>linux</li><li>win32</li><li>darwin</li></ul> |
109|| `platform_machine` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.machine()` | <ul><li>x86_64</li></ul> |
110|| `platform_python_implementation` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.python_implementation()` | <ul><li>CPython</li><li>Jython</li></ul> |
111|| `platform_release` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.release()` | <ul><li>1.8.0_51</li><li>3.14.1-x86_64-linode39</li></ul> |
112|| `platform_system` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.system()` | <ul><li>Linux</li><li>Windows</li><li>Darwin</li></ul> |
113|| `platform_version` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.version()` | <ul><li>10.0.19041</li><li>\#1 SMP Fri Apr 2 22:23:49 UTC 2021</li></ul> |
114|| `python_version` | `#!python import platform`<br>`'.'.join(platform.python_version_tuple()[:2])` | <ul><li>2.7</li><li>3.10</li></ul> |
115|| `python_full_version` | `#!python import platform`<br>`platform.python_version()` | <ul><li>2.7.18</li><li>3.11.0b1</li></ul> |
116|| `implementation_name` | `#!python import sys`<br>`sys.implementation.name` | <ul><li>cpython</li></ul> |
117|| `implementation_version` | See [here](https://peps.python.org/pep-0508/#environment-markers) | <ul><li>2.7.18</li><li>3.11.0b1</li></ul> |
118|
119|## Features
120|
121|You can select groups of [optional dependencies](metadata.md#optional) to install using the [extras](https://peps.python.org/pep-0508/#extras) syntax. For example, if a dependency named `foo` defined the following:
122|
123|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
124|[project.optional-dependencies]
125|crypto = [
126|  "PyJWT",
127|  "cryptography",
128|]
129|fastjson = [
130|  "orjson",
131|]
132|cli = [
133|  "prompt-toolkit",
134|  "colorama; platform_system == 'Windows'",
135|]
136|```
137|
138|You can select the `cli` and `crypto` features like so:
139|
140|```
141|foo[cli,crypto]==1.*
142|```
143|
144|Note that the features come immediately after the package name, before any [version specifiers](#version-specifiers).
145|
146|### Self-referential
147|
148|Feature groups can self-referentially extend others. For example, for a project called `awesome-project`, the `dev` feature group in the following `pyproject.toml` file would select everything in the `crypto` feature group, plus `black`:
149|
150|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
151|[project]
152|name = "awesome-project"
153|
154|[project.optional-dependencies]
155|crypto = [
156|  "PyJWT",
157|  "cryptography",
158|]
159|dev = [
160|  "awesome-project[crypto]",
161|  "black",
162|]
163|```
164|
165|## Direct references
166|
167|Instead of using normal [version specifiers](#version-specifiers) and fetching packages from an index like PyPI, you can define exact sources using [direct references](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#direct-references) with an explicit [URI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier#Syntax).
168|
169|Direct references are usually not meant to be used for dependencies of a published project but rather are used for defining [dependencies for an environment](environment/overview.md#dependencies).
170|
171|All direct reference types are prefixed by the package name like:
172|
173|```
174|<NAME> @ <REFERENCE>
175|```
176|
177|### Version control systems
178|
179|Various version control systems (VCS) are [supported](#supported-vcs) as long as the associated executable is available along your `PATH`.
180|
181|VCS direct references are defined using one of the following formats:
182|
183|```
184|<NAME> @ <SCHEME>://<PATH>
185|<NAME> @ <SCHEME>://<PATH>@<REVISION>
186|```
187|
188|You may also append a `#subdirectory=<PATH>` component for specifying the relative path to the Python package when it is not located at the root e.g. `#subdirectory=lib/foo`.
189|
190|For more information, refer to [this](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/vcs-support/).
191|
192|#### Supported VCS
193|
194|=== "Git"
195|    | Executable | Schemes | Revisions | Example |
196|    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
197|    | `git` | <ul><li><code>git+file</code></li><li><code>git+https</code></li><li><code>git+ssh</code></li><li><code>git+http</code> :warning:</li><li><code>git+git</code> :warning:</li><li><code>git</code> :warning:</li></ul> | <ul><li>Commit hash</li><li>Tag name</li><li>Branch name</li></ul> | `proj @ git+https://github.com/org/proj.git@v1` |
198|
199|=== "Mercurial"
200|    | Executable | Schemes | Revisions | Example |
201|    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
202|    | `hg` | <ul><li><code>hg+file</code></li><li><code>hg+https</code></li><li><code>hg+ssh</code></li><li><code>hg+http</code> :warning:</li><li><code>hg+static-http</code> :warning:</li></ul> | <ul><li>Revision hash</li><li>Revision number</li><li>Tag name</li><li>Branch name</li></ul> | `proj @ hg+file:///path/to/proj@v1` |
203|
204|=== "Subversion"
205|    | Executable | Schemes | Revisions | Example |
206|    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
207|    | `svn` | <ul><li><code>svn+https</code></li><li><code>svn+ssh</code></li><li><code>svn+http</code> :warning:</li><li><code>svn+svn</code> :warning:</li><li><code>svn</code> :warning:</li></ul> | <ul><li>Revision number</li></ul> | `proj @ svn+file:///path/to/proj` |
208|
209|=== "Bazaar"
210|    | Executable | Schemes | Revisions | Example |
211|    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
212|    | `bzr` | <ul><li><code>bzr+https</code></li><li><code>bzr+ssh</code></li><li><code>bzr+sftp</code></li><li><code>bzr+lp</code></li><li><code>bzr+http</code> :warning:</li><li><code>bzr+ftp</code> :warning:</li></ul> | <ul><li>Revision number</li><li>Tag name</li></ul> | `proj @ bzr+lp:proj@v1` |
213|
214|### Local
215|
216|You can install local packages with the `file` scheme in the following format:
217|
218|```
219|<NAME> @ file://<HOST>/<PATH>
220|```
221|
222|The `<HOST>` is only used on Windows systems, where it can refer to a network share. If omitted it is assumed to be `localhost` and the third slash must still be present.
223|
224|The `<PATH>` can refer to a source archive, a wheel, or a directory containing a Python package.
225|
226|| Type | Unix | Windows |
227|| --- | --- | --- |
228|| Source archive | `proj @ file:///path/to/pkg.tar.gz` | `proj @ file:///c:/path/to/pkg.tar.gz` |
229|| Wheel | `proj @ file:///path/to/pkg.whl` | `proj @ file:///c:/path/to/pkg.whl` |
230|| Directory | `proj @ file:///path/to/pkg` | `proj @ file:///c:/path/to/pkg` |
231|
232|!!! tip
233|    You may also specify paths relative to your project's root directory on all platforms by using [context formatting](context.md#paths):
234|
235|    ```
236|    <NAME> @ {root:uri}/pkg_inside_project
237|    <NAME> @ {root:parent:uri}/pkg_alongside_project
238|    ```
239|
240|### Remote
241|
242|You can install source archives and wheels by simply referring to a URL:
243|
244|```
245|black @ https://github.com/psf/black/archive/refs/tags/21.10b0.zip
246|pytorch @ https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu102/torch-1.10.0%2Bcu102-cp39-cp39-linux_x86_64.whl
247|```
248|
249|An expected hash value may be specified by appending a `#<HASH_ALGORITHM>=<EXPECTED_HASH>` component:
250|
251|```
252|requests @ https://github.com/psf/requests/archive/refs/tags/v2.26.0.zip#sha256=eb729a757f01c10546ebd179ae2aec852dd0d7f8ada2328ccf4558909d859985
253|```
254|
255|If the hash differs from the expected hash, the installation will fail.
256|
257|It is recommended that only hashes which are unconditionally provided by the latest version of the standard library's [hashlib module](https://docs.python.org/dev/library/hashlib.html) be used for hashes. As of Python 3.10, that list consists of:
258|
259|- `md5`
260|- `sha1`
261|- `sha224`
262|- `sha256`
263|- `sha384`
264|- `sha512`
265|- `blake2b`
266|- `blake2s`
267|
268|### Complex syntax
269|
270|The following is an example that uses [features](#features) and [environment markers](#environment-markers):
271|
272|```
273|pkg[feature1,feature2] @ <REFERENCE> ; python_version < "3.7"
274|```
275|
276|Note that the space before the semicolon is required.
277|
278|
279|## Sources
280|
281|Dependencies may be redirected to a local checkout, a Git branch, a URL, an alternate index, or a workspace member at install time, without changing the metadata your project publishes:
282|
283|```toml config-example
284|[project]
285|dependencies = ["foo"]
286|
287|[tool.hatch.sources]
288|foo = "./packages/foo"
289|```
290|
291|Sources are environment configuration, so each environment can redirect a dependency differently. See [environment sources](environment/sources.md) for the full reference.

71|def run_lock_workflow(
72|    app: Application,
73|    env_names: list[str],
74|    *,
75|    upgrade: bool,
76|    upgrade_package: tuple[str, ...],
77|    export_path: str | None,
78|    export_all_path: str | None,
79|    check: bool,
80|    explicit_env: str | None,
81|    skip_incompatible_envs: bool,
82|) -> None:
83|    """Shared implementation for ``hatch env lock`` and ``hatch dep lock``."""
84|    from hatch.config.constants import AppEnvVars
85|    from hatch.env.lock import (
86|        LockerNotFoundError,
87|        LockerUnsupportedError,
88|        environment_has_lock_inputs,
89|        generate_lockfile,
90|        lockfile_in_sync,
91|        merge_environment_lock_inputs,
92|        resolve_lockfile_path,
93|    )
94|    from hatch.utils.fs import Path
95|
96|    incompatible: dict[str, str] = {}
97|    lockfile_groups: dict[Path, list[str]] = {}
98|
99|    for env in env_names:
100|        environment = app.project.get_environment(env)
101|
102|        try:
103|            environment.check_compatibility()
104|        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
105|            if skip_incompatible_envs:
106|                incompatible[env] = str(e)
107|                continue
108|
109|            app.abort(f"Environment `{env}` is incompatible: {e}")
110|
111|        if explicit_env is not None and not environment.locked and not export_path and not export_all_path:
112|            app.abort(
113|                f"Environment `{explicit_env}` is not configured with `locked = true`. "
114|                f"Use `--export <path>` to generate a lockfile, "
115|                f"or set `locked = true` on the environment (or `lock-envs = true` globally)."
116|            )
117|
118|        if export_path:
119|            output_path = Path(export_path)
120|        elif export_all_path:
121|            safe_name = environment.name.replace(".", "-")
122|            filename = "pylock.toml" if environment.name == "default" else f"pylock.{safe_name}.toml"
123|            output_path = Path(export_all_path) / filename
124|        else:
125|            output_path = resolve_lockfile_path(environment)
126|
127|        if check:
128|            if not output_path.is_file():
129|                app.abort(f"Lockfile does not exist: {output_path}")
130|        elif not environment_has_lock_inputs(environment):
131|            app.display_warning(f"Environment `{env}` has no dependencies to lock")
132|            continue
133|
134|        lockfile_groups.setdefault(output_path, []).append(env)
135|
136|    for output_path, envs in lockfile_groups.items():
137|        environment, merged_deps, merged_extras, merged_groups, display_name = merge_environment_lock_inputs(
138|            app.project, envs, app.abort
139|        )
140|
141|        try:
142|            if check:
143|                with app.status(f"Checking lockfile for: {display_name}"):
144|                    app.project.prepare_environment(environment, keep_env=bool(os.environ.get(AppEnvVars.KEEP_ENV)))
145|                    if not lockfile_in_sync(
146|                        environment,
147|                        output_path,
148|                        upgrade=upgrade,
149|                        upgrade_packages=upgrade_package,
150|                        deps_override=merged_deps,
151|                        lock_extras=merged_extras,
152|                        lock_groups=merged_groups,
153|                    ):
154|                        app.abort(f"Lockfile is not up to date: {output_path}")
155|                app.display(f"Lockfile is up to date: {output_path}")
156|                continue
157|
158|            with app.status(f"Locking environment: {display_name}"):
159|                app.project.prepare_environment(environment, keep_env=bool(os.environ.get(AppEnvVars.KEEP_ENV)))
160|                generate_lockfile(
161|                    environment,
162|                    output_path,
163|                    upgrade=upgrade,
164|                    upgrade_packages=upgrade_package,
165|                    deps_override=merged_deps,
166|                    lock_extras=merged_extras,
167|                    lock_groups=merged_groups,
168|                )
169|
170|            app.display(f"Wrote lockfile: {output_path}")
171|        except LockerNotFoundError as e:
172|            app.abort(str(e))
173|        except LockerUnsupportedError as e:
174|            app.abort(str(e))
175|
176|    if incompatible:
177|        num_incompatible = len(incompatible)
178|        app.display_warning(
179|            f"Skipped {num_incompatible} incompatible environment{'s' if num_incompatible > 1 else ''}:"
180|        )
181|        for env, reason in incompatible.items():
182|            app.display_warning(f"{env} -> {reason}")

187|@click.option("--upgrade", "-U", is_flag=True, help="Upgrade all packages")
188|@click.option("--upgrade-package", "-P", multiple=True, help="Upgrade specific package(s)")
189|@click.option("--export", "export_path", type=click.Path(), default=None, help="Export lockfile to a custom path")

201|    *,
202|    env_name: str | None,

205|    export_path: str | None,
206|    export_all_path: str | None,
207|    check: bool,
208|):
209|    """Generate lockfiles for environments.

211|    When called without arguments, locks all environments that have `locked = true`
212|    in their configuration. When called with ENV_NAME, locks that specific environment.
213|    """
214|    app.ensure_environment_plugin_dependencies()
215|
216|    if export_path and export_all_path:
217|        app.abort("Cannot use both `--export` and `--export-all`")
218|
219|    if export_all_path:
220|        env_names = [*app.project.config.envs, *app.project.config.internal_envs]
221|        explicit_env = None
222|        skip_incompatible = True
223|    elif env_name is not None:
224|        env_names = app.project.expand_environments(env_name)

227|        explicit_env = env_name
228|        skip_incompatible = env_name in app.project.config.matrices
229|    else:
230|        env_names = []

1|# Environment configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|All environments are defined as sections within the `tool.hatch.envs` table.
6|
7|```toml config-example
8|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
9|```
10|
11|The [storage location](../hatch.md#environments) for environments is completely configurable.
12|
13|Unless an environment is explicitly selected on the command line, the `default` environment will be used. The [type](#type) of this environment defaults to `virtual`.
14|
15|!!! info
16|    Environments prefixed by `hatch-` are used for special purposes e.g. [testing](../internal/testing.md).
17|
18|## Inheritance
19|
20|All environments inherit from the environment defined by its `template` option, which defaults to `default`.
21|
22|So for the following configuration:
23|
24|```toml config-example
25|[tool.hatch.envs.foo]
26|type = "baz"
27|skip-install = true
28|
29|[tool.hatch.envs.bar]
30|template = "foo"
31|skip-install = false
32|```
33|
34|the environment `bar` will be of type `baz` with `skip-install` set to `false`.
35|
36|!!! note
37|    Environments do not inherit [matrices](advanced.md#matrix).
38|
39|### Self-referential environments
40|
41|You can disable inheritance by setting `template` to the environment's own name:
42|
43|```toml config-example
44|[tool.hatch.envs.foo]
45|template = "foo"
46|```
47|
48|### Detached environments
49|
50|A common use case is standalone environments that do not require inheritance nor the installation of the project, such as for linting or sometimes building documentation. Enabling the `detached` option will make the environment [self-referential](#self-referential-environments) and will [skip project installation](#skip-install):
51|
52|```toml config-example
53|[tool.hatch.envs.lint]
54|detached = true
55|```
56|
57|## Dependencies
58|
59|You can install [dependencies](../dependency.md) in addition to the ones defined by your [project's metadata](../metadata.md#dependencies). Entries support [context formatting](advanced.md#context-formatting).
60|
61|```toml config-example
62|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
63|dependencies = [
64|  "coverage[toml]",
65|  "pytest",
66|  "pytest-cov",
67|  "pytest-mock",
68|]
69|```
70|
71|If you define environments with dependencies that only slightly differ from their [inherited environments](#inheritance), you can use the `extra-dependencies` option to avoid redeclaring the `dependencies` option:
72|
73|```toml config-example
74|[tool.hatch.envs.default]
75|dependencies = [
76|  "foo",
77|  "bar",
78|]
79|
80|[tool.hatch.envs.experimental]
81|extra-dependencies = [
82|  "baz",
83|]
84|```
85|
86|!!! tip
87|    Hatch uses [pip](https://github.com/pypa/pip) to install dependencies so any [configuration](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/configuration/) it supports Hatch does as well. For example, if you wanted to only use a private repository you could set the `PIP_INDEX_URL` [environment variable](#environment-variables).
88|
89|!!! tip
90|    To redirect a dependency to a local path, Git repository, URL, alternate index, or workspace member without altering your published metadata, see [sources](sources.md). Each environment inherits the sources of its template and may override individual entries, and all sources can be disabled by setting the `HATCH_NO_SOURCES` environment variable.
91|
92|## Installation
93|
94|### Features (extras) ### {: #features }
95|
96|If your project defines [optional dependencies](../metadata.md#optional), you can select which groups to install using the `features` option:
97|
98|```toml config-example
99|[tool.hatch.envs.nightly]
100|features = [
101|  "server",
102|  "grpc",
103|]
104|```
105|
106|!!! note
107|    Features/optional dependencies are also known as `extras` in other tools.
108|
109|### Dependency Groups
110|
111|[Dependency groups](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/dependency-groups/#dependency-groups) provide a uniform way to organize related development dependencies. See [advanced usage](advanced.md#dependency-groups) for more details on dependency group features like including other groups.
112|
113|You can include dependency-groups in your hatch environments using the `[dependency-groups]` array:
114|
115|```toml config-example
116|[dependency-groups]
117|test = [
118|  "pytest>=7.0.0",
119|  "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
120|]
121|
122|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
123|dependency-groups = [
124|  "test",
125|]
126|```
127|
128|### Dev mode
129|
130|By default, environments will always reflect the current state of your project on disk, for example, by installing it in editable mode in a Python environment. Set `dev-mode` to `false` to disable this behavior and have your project installed only upon creation of a new environment. From then on, you need to manage your project installation manually.
131|
132|```toml config-example
133|[tool.hatch.envs.static]
134|dev-mode = false
135|```
136|
137|### Skip install
138|
139|By default, environments will install your project during creation. To ignore this step, set `skip-install` to `true`:
140|
141|```toml config-example
142|[tool.hatch.envs.lint]
143|skip-install = true
144|```
145|
146|## Environment variables
147|
148|### Defined
149|
150|You can define environment variables with the `env-vars` option:
151|
152|```toml config-example
153|[tool.hatch.envs.docs]
154|dependencies = [
155|  "mkdocs"
156|]
157|[tool.hatch.envs.docs.env-vars]
158|SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH = "1580601600"
159|```
160|
161|Values support [context formatting](advanced.md#context-formatting).
162|
163|### Filters
164|
165|By default, environments will have access to all environment variables. You can filter with wildcard patterns using the `env-include`/`env-exclude` options:
166|
167|```toml config-example
168|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
169|env-include = [
170|  "FOO*",
171|]
172|env-exclude = [
173|  "BAR",
174|]
175|```
176|
177|Exclusion patterns take precedence but will never affect [defined](#defined) environment variables.
178|
179|## Scripts
180|
181|You can define named scripts that may be [executed](../../environment.md#command-execution) or referenced at the beginning of other scripts. [Context formatting](advanced.md#context-formatting) is supported.
182|
183|For example, in the following configuration:
184|
185|```toml config-example
186|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
187|dependencies = [
188|  "coverage[toml]",
189|  "pytest",
190|  "pytest-cov",
191|  "pytest-mock",
192|]
193|[tool.hatch.envs.test.scripts]
194|run-coverage = "pytest --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov=pkg --cov=tests"
195|run = "run-coverage --no-cov"
196|```
197|
198|the `run` script would be expanded to:
199|
200|```
201|pytest --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov=pkg --cov=tests --no-cov
202|```
203|
204|Scripts can also be defined as an array of strings.
205|
206|```toml config-example
207|[tool.hatch.envs.style]
208|detached = true
209|dependencies = [
210|  "flake8",
211|  "black",
212|  "isort",
213|]
214|[tool.hatch.envs.style.scripts]
215|check = [
216|  "flake8 .",
217|  "black --check --diff .",
218|  "isort --check-only --diff .",
219|]
220|fmt = [
221|  "isort .",
222|  "black .",
223|  "check",
224|]
225|```
226|
227|Similar to [make](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/manual/html_node/Errors.html), you can ignore the exit code of commands that start with `-` (a hyphen). For example, the script `error` defined by the following configuration would halt after the second command with `3` as the exit code:
228|
229|```toml config-example
230|[tool.hatch.envs.test.scripts]
231|error = [
232|  "- exit 1",
233|  "exit 3",
234|  "exit 0",
235|]
236|```
237|
238|### Extra scripts
239|
240|Individual scripts [inherit](#inheritance) from parent environments just like options. To guarantee that individual scripts do not override those defined by parent environments, you can use the `extra-scripts` option instead which is only capable of adding scripts that have not been defined.
241|
242|## Commands
243|
244|All commands are able to use any defined [scripts](#scripts). Also like scripts, [context formatting](advanced.md#context-formatting) is supported and the exit code of commands that start with a hyphen will be ignored.
245|
246|### Pre-install
247|
248|You can run commands immediately before environments [install](#skip-install) your project.
249|
250|```toml config-example
251|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
252|pre-install-commands = [
253|  "...",
254|]
255|```
256|
257|### Post-install
258|
259|You can run commands immediately after environments [install](#skip-install) your project.
260|
261|```toml config-example
262|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
263|post-install-commands = [
264|  "...",
265|]
266|```
267|
268|## Python version
269|
270|The `python` option specifies which version of Python to use, or an absolute path to a Python interpreter:
271|
272|```toml config-example
273|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
274|python = "3.10"
275|```
276|
277|All [environment types](#type) should respect this option.
278|
279|## Supported platforms
280|
281|The `platforms` option indicates the operating systems with which the environment is compatible:
282|
283|```toml config-example
284|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
285|platforms = ["linux", "windows", "macos"]
286|```
287|
288|The following platforms are supported:
289|
290|- `linux`
291|- `windows`
292|- `macos`
293|
294|If unspecified, the environment is assumed to be compatible with all platforms.
295|
296|## Locking
297|
298|Hatch can generate [PEP 751](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/) lockfiles (`pylock.toml`) for environments. Lockfiles capture the exact versions of all resolved dependencies, ensuring reproducible installations.
299|
300|### Locked
301|
302|Set `locked` to `true` to enable automatic lockfile generation for an environment. When enabled, a lockfile will be generated whenever the environment is created or its dependencies change.
303|
304|```toml config-example
305|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
306|locked = true
307|dependencies = [
308|  "pytest",
309|  "pytest-cov",
310|]
311|```
312|
313|The default value is `false` unless overridden by the global [`lock-envs`](#lock-envs) setting.
314|
315|### Locker plugin ### {: #locker }
316|
317|Select which [dependency locker](../../plugins/locker.md) runs **generate**, **in_sync**, and **apply_lock** (defaults follow the environment installer: `uv` with UV, otherwise `pip`).
318|
319|!!! note
320|    Locker capabilities can differ. The built-in `pip` locker does not currently implement `apply_lock`, so lockfile application with [`dep sync`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-sync) requires the `uv` locker.
321|
322|Global default:
323|
324|```toml config-example
325|[tool.hatch]
326|locker = "uv"
327|```
328|
329|Per environment (overrides `tool.hatch.locker`):
330|
331|```toml config-example
332|[tool.hatch.envs.docs]
333|locker = "pip"
334|```
335|
336|### Lock filename ### {: #lock-filename }
337|
338|By default, lockfiles are named following the [PEP 751](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/) convention: `pylock.toml` for the `default` environment and `pylock.<ENV_NAME>.toml` for all others. You can override this with the `lock-filename` option:
339|
340|```toml config-example
341|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
342|lock-filename = "locks/test-requirements.lock"
343|```
344|
345|### Global lock-envs ### {: #lock-envs }
346|
347|You can enable locking for all environments at once by setting `lock-envs` to `true` at the top level of your Hatch configuration:
348|
349|```toml config-example
350|[tool.hatch]
351|lock-envs = true
352|```
353|
354|This acts as the default value for each environment's [`locked`](#locked) option. Individual environments can still opt out by explicitly setting `locked = false`:
355|
356|```toml config-example
357|[tool.hatch]
358|lock-envs = true
359|
360|[tool.hatch.envs.docs]
361|locked = false
362|```
363|
364|See the [lockfile how-to guide](../../how-to/environment/lockfiles.md) for practical usage examples.
365|
366|## Description
367|
368|The `description` option is purely informational and is displayed in the output of the [`env show`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-show) command:
369|
370|```toml config-example
371|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
372|description = """
373|Lorem ipsum ...
374|"""
375|```
376|
377|## Type
378|
379|An environment's `type` determines which [environment plugin](../../plugins/environment/reference.md) will be used for management. The only built-in environment type is [`virtual`](../../plugins/environment/virtual.md), which uses virtual Python environments.

1|from __future__ import annotations

3|import os
4|import signal
5|import sys
6|from functools import cached_property
7|from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast
8|
9|from hatch.cli.terminal import Terminal
10|from hatch.config.user import ConfigFile, RootConfig
11|from hatch.project.core import Project
12|from hatch.utils.fs import Path
13|from hatch.utils.platform import Platform
14|from hatch.utils.runner import ExecutionContext
15|
16|if TYPE_CHECKING:
17|    from collections.abc import Generator
18|
19|    from hatch.dep.core import Dependency
20|    from hatch.env.plugin.interface import EnvironmentInterface
21|
22|
23|class Application(Terminal):
24|    def __init__(self, exit_func, *args, **kwargs):
25|        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
26|        self.platform = Platform(self.output)
27|        self.__exit_func = exit_func
28|
29|        self.config_file = ConfigFile()
30|        self.quiet = self.verbosity < 0
31|        self.verbose = self.verbosity > 0
32|
33|        # Lazily set these as we acquire more knowledge about the environment
34|        self.data_dir = cast(Path, None)
35|        self.cache_dir = cast(Path, None)
36|        self.project = cast(Project, None)
37|        self.env = cast(str, None)
38|        self.env_active = cast(str, None)
39|
40|    @property
41|    def plugins(self):
42|        return self.project.plugin_manager
43|
44|    @property
45|    def config(self) -> RootConfig:
46|        return self.config_file.model
47|
48|    def get_environment(self, env_name: str | None = None) -> EnvironmentInterface:
49|        return self.project.get_environment(env_name)
50|
51|    def prepare_environment(self, environment: EnvironmentInterface, *, keep_env: bool = False):
52|        self.project.prepare_environment(environment, keep_env=keep_env)
53|
54|    def run_shell_commands(self, context: ExecutionContext) -> None:
55|        with context.env.command_context():
56|            try:
57|                resolved_commands = list(context.env.resolve_commands(context.shell_commands))
58|            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
59|                self.abort(str(e))
60|
61|            first_error_code = None
62|            should_display_command = not context.hide_commands and (self.verbose or len(resolved_commands) > 1)
63|            for i, raw_command in enumerate(resolved_commands, 1):
64|                if should_display_command:
65|                    self.display_info(f"{context.source} [{i}] | {raw_command}")
66|
67|                command = raw_command
68|                continue_on_error = context.force_continue
69|                if raw_command.startswith("- "):
70|                    continue_on_error = True
71|                    command = command[2:]
72|
73|                # Ignore SIGINT in the parent process while the child command runs so that
74|                # only the child handles Ctrl-C.  The terminal sends SIGINT to the entire
75|                # foreground process group; without this the parent raises KeyboardInterrupt
76|                # and aborts even though the child (e.g. a Python REPL) may choose to stay
77|                # alive.  The child's exit code is still used to determine success/failure.
78|                # A handler that does nothing is used rather than `signal.SIG_IGN` because
79|                # handled signals are reset to their default action when the child is
80|                # executed whereas ignored signals stay ignored, which would otherwise make
81|                # the child itself unable to be interrupted.
82|                original_sigint = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)
83|                try:
84|                    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda *_: None)
85|                    process = context.env.run_shell_command(command)
86|                finally:
87|                    # Restore the original handler in finally so the parent stays
88|                    # responsive to Ctrl-C even if the child raises or is cancelled.
89|                    # Don't hoist this out of the finally block.
90|                    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, original_sigint)
91|                sys.stdout.flush()
92|                sys.stderr.flush()
93|                if process.returncode:
94|                    first_error_code = first_error_code or process.returncode
95|                    if continue_on_error:
96|                        continue
97|
98|                    if context.show_code_on_error:
99|                        self.abort(f"Failed with exit code: {process.returncode}", code=process.returncode)
100|                    else:
101|                        self.abort(code=process.returncode)
102|
103|            if first_error_code and context.force_continue:
104|                self.abort(code=first_error_code)
105|
106|    def runner_context(
107|        self,
108|        environments: list[str],
109|        *,
110|        ignore_compat: bool = False,
111|        display_header: bool = False,
112|        keep_env: bool = False,
113|    ) -> Generator[ExecutionContext, None, None]:
114|        if self.verbose or len(environments) > 1:
115|            display_header = True
116|
117|        any_compatible = False
118|        incompatible = {}
119|        with self.project.ensure_cwd():
120|            for env_name in environments:
121|                environment = self.get_environment(env_name)
122|                if not environment.exists():
123|                    try:
124|                        environment.check_compatibility()
125|                    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
126|                        if ignore_compat:
127|                            incompatible[environment.name] = str(e)
128|                            continue
129|
130|                        self.abort(f"Environment `{env_name}` is incompatible: {e}")
131|
132|                any_compatible = True
133|                if display_header:
134|                    self.display_header(environment.name)
135|
136|                context = ExecutionContext(environment)
137|                yield context
138|
139|                self.prepare_environment(environment, keep_env=keep_env)
140|                self.execute_context(context)
141|
142|        if incompatible:
143|            num_incompatible = len(incompatible)
144|            padding = "\n" if any_compatible else ""
145|            self.display_warning(
146|                f"{padding}Skipped {num_incompatible} incompatible environment{'s' if num_incompatible > 1 else ''}:"
147|            )
148|            for env_name, reason in incompatible.items():
149|                self.display_warning(f"{env_name} -> {reason}")
150|
151|    def execute_context(self, context: ExecutionContext) -> None:
152|        from hatch.utils.structures import EnvVars
153|
154|        with EnvVars(context.env_vars):
155|            self.run_shell_commands(context)
156|
157|    def ensure_environment_plugin_dependencies(self) -> None:
158|        self.ensure_plugin_dependencies(
159|            self.project.config.env_requires_complex, wait_message="Syncing environment plugin requirements"
160|        )
161|
162|    def ensure_plugin_dependencies(self, dependencies: list[Dependency], *, wait_message: str) -> None:
163|        if not dependencies:
164|            return
165|
166|        from hatch.dep.sync import InstalledDistributions
167|        from hatch.env.utils import add_verbosity_flag
168|
169|        if app_path := os.environ.get("PYAPP"):
170|            from hatch.utils.env import PythonInfo
171|
172|            management_command = os.environ.get("PYAPP_COMMAND_NAME", "self")
173|            executable = self.platform.check_command_output([app_path, management_command, "python-path"]).strip()
174|            python_info = PythonInfo(self.platform, executable=executable)
175|            distributions = InstalledDistributions(sys_path=python_info.sys_path)
176|            if distributions.dependencies_in_sync(dependencies):
177|                return
178|            pip_command = [app_path, management_command, "pip", "install", "--disable-pip-version-check"]
179|        else:
180|            distributions = InstalledDistributions()
181|            if distributions.dependencies_in_sync(dependencies):
182|                return
183|
184|            from uv import find_uv_bin
185|
186|            uv_bin = find_uv_bin()
187|            pip_command = [uv_bin, "pip", "install", "--python", sys.executable]
188|
189|        # Default to -1 verbosity
190|        add_verbosity_flag(pip_command, self.verbosity, adjustment=-1)
191|
192|        pip_command.extend(str(dependency) for dependency in dependencies)
193|
194|        with self.status(wait_message):
195|            self.platform.check_command(pip_command)
196|
197|    def get_env_directory(self, environment_type):
198|        directories = self.config.dirs.env
199|
200|        if environment_type in directories:
201|            path = Path(directories[environment_type]).expand()
202|            if os.path.isabs(path):
203|                return path
204|
205|            return self.project.location / path
206|
207|        return self.data_dir / "env" / environment_type
208|
209|    def get_python_manager(self, directory: str | None = None):
210|        from hatch.python.core import PythonManager
211|
212|        configured_dir = directory or self.config.dirs.python
213|        if configured_dir == "isolated":
214|            return PythonManager(self.data_dir / "pythons")
215|
216|        return PythonManager(Path(configured_dir).expand())
217|
218|    @cached_property
219|    def shell_data(self) -> tuple[str, str]:
220|        from hatch.utils.shells import detect_shell
221|
222|        return detect_shell(self.platform)
223|
224|    def abort(self, text="", code=1, **kwargs):
225|        if text:
226|            self.display_error(text, **kwargs)
227|        self.__exit_func(code)
