1|# Advanced environment configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|## Context formatting
6|
7|All environments support the following extra [context formatting](../context.md) fields:
8|
9|| Field | Description |
10|| --- | --- |
11|| `env_name` | The name of the environment |
12|| `env_type` | The [type](overview.md#type) of environment |
13|| `matrix` | Its modifier selects the value of that matrix variable. If the environment is not part of a matrix or was not generated with the variable, you must specify a default value as an additional modifier e.g. `{matrix:version:v1.0.0}`. |
14|| `verbosity` | The integer verbosity value of Hatch. A `flag` modifier is supported that will render the value as a CLI flag e.g. `-2` becomes `-qq`, `1` becomes `-v`, and `0` becomes an empty string. An additional flag integer modifier may be used to adjust the verbosity level. For example, if you wanted to make a command quiet by default, you could use `{verbosity:flag:-1}` within the command. |
15|| `args` | For [executed commands](../../environment.md#command-execution) only, any extra command line arguments with an optional default modifier if none were provided |
16|
17|## Matrix
18|
19|Environments can define a series of matrices with the `matrix` option:
20|
21|```toml config-example
22|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
23|dependencies = [
24|  "pytest"
25|]
26|
27|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
28|python = ["3.10", "3.11"]
29|version = ["42", "3.14"]
30|
31|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
32|python = ["3.11", "3.12"]
33|version = ["9000"]
34|feature = ["foo", "bar"]
35|```
36|
37|Doing so will result in the product of each variable combination being its own environment.
38|
39|### Naming
40|
41|The name of the generated environments will be the variable values of each combination separated by hyphens, altogether prefixed by `<ENV_NAME>.`. For example, the following configuration:
42|
43|```toml config-example
44|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
45|version = ["42"]
46|feature = ["foo", "bar"]
47|```
48|
49|would indicate the following unique environments:
50|
51|```
52|test.42-foo
53|test.42-bar
54|```
55|
56|The exceptions to this format are described below.
57|
58|#### Python variables
59|
60|If the variables `py` or `python` are specified, then they will rank first in the product result and will be prefixed by `py` if the value is not. For example, the following configuration:
61|
62|```toml config-example
63|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
64|version = ["42"]
65|python = ["3.9", "pypy3"]
66|```
67|
68|would generate the following environments:
69|
70|```
71|test.py3.9-42
72|test.pypy3-42
73|```
74|
75|!!! note
76|    The value of this variable sets the [Python version](overview.md#python-version).
77|
78|#### Name formatting
79|
80|You can set the `matrix-name-format` option to modify how each variable part is formatted which recognizes the placeholders `{variable}` and `{value}`. For example, the following configuration:
81|
82|```toml config-example
83|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
84|matrix-name-format = "{variable}_{value}"
85|
86|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
87|version = ["42"]
88|feature = ["foo", "bar"]
89|```
90|
91|would produce the following environments:
92|
93|```
94|test.version_42-feature_foo
95|test.version_42-feature_bar
96|```
97|
98|By default this option is set to `{value}`.
99|
100|#### Default environment
101|
102|If the `default` environment defines matrices, then the generated names will not be prefixed by the environment name. This can be useful for projects that only need a single series of matrices without any standalone environments.
103|
104|### Selection
105|
106|Rather than [selecting](../../environment.md#selection) a single generated environment, you can select the root environment to target all of them. For example, if you have the following configuration:
107|
108|```toml config-example
109|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
110|dependencies = [
111|  "coverage[toml]",
112|  "pytest",
113|  "pytest-cov",
114|]
115|
116|[tool.hatch.envs.test.scripts]
117|cov = 'pytest --cov-report=term-missing --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov=pkg --cov=tests'
118|
119|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
120|python = ["3.11", "3.12"]
121|version = ["42", "3.14"]
122|```
123|
124|you could then run your tests consecutively in all 4 environments with:
125|
126|```
127|hatch run test:cov
128|```
129|
130|## Dependency Groups
131|
132|Environments can use dependency groups[^1] using the environment `dependency-groups` array:
133|
134|```toml config-example
135|[dependency-groups]
136|test = [
137|  "pytest>=7.0.0",
138|  "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
139|]
140|lint = [
141|  "black",
142|  "ruff",
143|  "mypy",
144|]
145|# Groups can include other groups
146|dev = [
147|  {include-group = "test"},
148|  {include-group = "lint"},
149|  "pre-commit",
150|]
151|
152|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
153|dependency-groups = ["test"]
154|
155|[tool.hatch.envs.lint]
156|dependency-groups = ["lint"]
157|
158|[tool.hatch.envs.dev]
159|dependency-groups = ["dev"]
160|```
161|
162|The `dependency-groups` array specifies which dependency groups to include in the environment's dependencies. This is particularly useful for organizing related dependencies and including them in appropriate environments.
163|
164|### Combining with Other Dependencies
165|
166|Dependency groups can be combined with other dependency mechanisms:
167|
168|```toml config-example
169|[project]
170|name = "my-app"
171|version = "0.1.0"
172|dependencies = [
173|  "requests>=2.28.0",
174|]
175|
176|[dependency-groups]
177|test = ["pytest>=7.0.0"]
178|docs = ["sphinx>=7.0.0"]
179|
180|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
181|# Include the test dependency group
182|dependency-groups = ["test"]
183|# Add environment-specific dependencies
184|dependencies = [
185|  "coverage[toml]>=7.0.0",
186|]
187|```
188|
189|In this example, the test environment would include:
190|1. Project dependencies (`requests>=2.28.0`)
191|2. The test dependency group (`pytest>=7.0.0`)
192|3. Environment-specific dependencies (`coverage[toml]>=7.0.0`)
193|
194|## Option overrides
195|
196|You can modify options based on the conditions of different sources like [matrix variables](#matrix-variable-overrides) with the `overrides` table, using [dotted key](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0#table) syntax for each declaration:
197|
198|```toml config-example
199|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>.overrides]
200|<SOURCE>.<CONDITION>.<OPTION> = <VALUE>
201|```
202|
203|The [type](#types) of the selected option determines the types of values.
204|
205|### Platform overrides
206|
207|Options can be modified based on the current platform using the `platform` source.
208|
209|```toml config-example
210|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
211|platform.windows.scripts = [
212|  'run=pytest -m "not io_uring"',
213|]
214|```
215|
216|The following platforms are supported:
217|
218|- `linux`
219|- `windows`
220|- `macos`
221|
222|### Environment variable overrides
223|
224|Environment variables can modify options using the `env` source.
225|
226|```toml config-example
227|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
228|env.GITHUB_ACTIONS.dev-mode = { value = false, if = ["true"] }
229|```
230|
231|### Matrix variable overrides
232|
233|The [matrix](#matrix) variables used to generate each environment can be used to modify options within using the `matrix` source.
234|
235|```toml config-example
236|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
237|matrix.version.env-vars = "PRODUCT_VERSION"
238|matrix.auth.features = [
239|  { value = "oauth", if = ["oauth2"] },
240|  { value = "kerberos", if = ["kerberos"] },
241|]
242|
243|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
244|python = ["3.11", "3.12"]
245|version = ["legacy", "latest"]
246|auth = ["oauth2", "kerberos", "noauth"]
247|```
248|
249|### Name overrides
250|
251|When a [matrix](#matrix) is defined, the `name` source can be used for regular expression matching on the generated name, minus the prefix for non-[default](#default-environment) environments.
252|
253|```toml config-example
254|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
255|name."^0".env-vars = "TESTING_UNSTABLE=true"
256|
257|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
258|version = ["0.1.0", "0.2.0", "1.0.0"]
259|```
260|
261|### Types
262|
263|- Literal types like strings for the [Python version](overview.md#python-version) or booleans for [skipping installation](overview.md#skip-install) can be set using the value itself, an inline table, or an array. For example:
264|
265|    ```toml config-example
266|    [tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
267|    matrix.foo.python = "3.10"
268|    matrix.bar.skip-install = { value = true, if = ["..."] }
269|    env.CI.dev-mode = [
270|      { value = false, if = ["..."] },
271|      true,
272|    ]
273|    ```
274|
275|    For arrays, the first allowed value will be used.
276|
277|- Array types like [dependencies](overview.md#dependencies) or [commands](overview.md#commands) can be appended to using an array of strings or inline tables. For example:
278|
279|    ```toml config-example
280|    [tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
281|    matrix.foo.dependencies = [
282|      "httpx2",
283|      { value = "cryptography" },
284|    ]
285|    ```
286|
287|- Mapping types like [environment variables](overview.md#environment-variables) or [scripts](overview.md#scripts) can have keys set using a string, or an array of strings or inline tables. For example:
288|
289|    ```toml config-example
290|    [tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
291|    matrix.foo.env-vars = "KEY=VALUE"
292|    matrix.bar.env-vars = [
293|      "KEY1=VALUE1",
294|      { key = "KEY2", value = "VALUE2" },
295|    ]
296|    ```
297|
298|    If the value is missing (no `=` for strings, no `value` key for inline tables), then the value will be set to the value of the source condition.
299|
300|### Overwriting
301|
302|Rather than supplementing the values within mapping types or array types, you can overwrite the option as a whole by prefixing the name with `set-`:
303|
304|```toml config-example
305|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
306|matrix.foo.set-platforms = ["macos", "linux"]
307|```
308|
309|When overwriting entire options or keys within mappings, override sources are applied in the following order:
310|
311|1. [platform](#platform-overrides)
312|2. [environment variables](#environment-variable-overrides)
313|3. [matrix variables](#matrix-variable-overrides)
314|4. [names](#name-overrides)
315|
316|### Conditions
317|
318|You may specify certain extra keys for any inline table that will determine whether or not to apply that entry. These modifiers may be combined with others and any negative evaluation will immediately cause the entry to be skipped.
319|
320|#### Allowed values
321|
322|The `if` key represents the allowed values for that condition. If the value of the condition is not listed, then that entry will not be applied:
323|
324|```toml config-example
325|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
326|matrix.version.python = { value = "pypy", if = ["3.14"] }
327|matrix.version.env-vars = [
328|  { key = "KEY1", value = "VALUE1", if = ["42"] },
329|  { key = "KEY2", value = "VALUE2", if = ["3.14"] },
330|]
331|
332|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
333|version = ["42", "3.14"]
334|```
335|
336|#### Specific platforms
337|
338|The `platform` key represents the desired platforms. If the current platform is not listed, then that entry will not be applied:
339|
340|```toml config-example
341|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
342|env.EXPERIMENTAL.python = { value = "pypy", if = ["1"], platform = ["macos"] }
343|matrix.version.env-vars = [
344|  { key = "KEY1", value = "VALUE1", if = ["42"], platform = ["linux"] },
345|  { key = "KEY2", value = "VALUE2", if = ["3.14"] },
346|]
347|
348|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
349|version = ["42", "3.14"]
350|```
351|
352|#### Required environment variables
353|
354|The `env` key represents the required environment variables. If any of the listed environment variables are not set or the defined value does not match, then that entry will not be applied:
355|
356|```toml config-example
357|[tool.hatch.envs.test.overrides]
358|platform.windows.python = { value = "pypy", env = ["EXPERIMENTAL"] }
359|matrix.version.env-vars = [
360|  { key = "KEY1", value = "VALUE1", if = ["42"], env = ["FOO", "BAR=BAZ"] },
361|  { key = "KEY2", value = "VALUE2", if = ["3.14"] },
362|]
363|
364|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
365|version = ["42", "3.14"]
366|```

1|from __future__ import annotations
2|
3|from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
4|
5|import click
6|
7|if TYPE_CHECKING:
8|    from hatch.cli.application import Application
9|
10|
11|@click.command(short_help="Show the available environments")
12|@click.argument("envs", required=False, nargs=-1)
13|@click.option("--ascii", "force_ascii", is_flag=True, help="Whether or not to only use ASCII characters")
14|@click.option("--json", "as_json", is_flag=True, help="Whether or not to output in JSON format")
15|@click.option("--internal", "-i", is_flag=True, help="Show internal environments")
16|@click.option("--hide-titles", is_flag=True, hidden=True)
17|@click.pass_obj
18|def show(
19|    app: Application,
20|    *,
21|    envs: tuple[str, ...],
22|    force_ascii: bool,
23|    as_json: bool,
24|    internal: bool,
25|    hide_titles: bool,
26|):
27|    """Show the available environments."""
28|    app.ensure_environment_plugin_dependencies()
29|
30|    from hatch.config.constants import AppEnvVars
31|
32|    if as_json:
33|        import json
34|
35|        contextual_config = {}
36|        for environments in (app.project.config.envs, app.project.config.internal_envs):
37|            for env_name, config in environments.items():
38|                environment = app.project.get_environment(env_name)
39|                new_config = contextual_config[env_name] = dict(config)
40|
41|                env_vars = dict(environment.env_vars)
42|                env_vars.pop(AppEnvVars.ENV_ACTIVE)
43|                if env_vars:
44|                    new_config["env-vars"] = env_vars
45|
46|                num_dependencies = len(config.get("dependencies", []))
47|                dependencies = environment.environment_dependencies[:num_dependencies]
48|                if dependencies:
49|                    new_config["dependencies"] = dependencies
50|
51|                extra_dependencies = environment.environment_dependencies[num_dependencies:]
52|                if extra_dependencies:
53|                    new_config["extra-dependencies"] = extra_dependencies
54|
55|                if environment.pre_install_commands:
56|                    new_config["pre-install-commands"] = list(
57|                        environment.resolve_commands(environment.pre_install_commands)
58|                    )
59|
60|                if environment.post_install_commands:
61|                    new_config["post-install-commands"] = list(
62|                        environment.resolve_commands(environment.post_install_commands)
63|                    )
64|
65|                if environment.scripts:
66|                    new_config["scripts"] = {
67|                        script: list(environment.resolve_commands([script])) for script in environment.scripts
68|                    }
69|
70|        app.display(json.dumps(contextual_config, separators=(",", ":")))
71|        return
72|
73|    from hatch.dep.core import Dependency, InvalidDependencyError
74|    from hatchling.metadata.utils import get_normalized_dependency, normalize_project_name
75|
76|    if internal:
77|        target_standalone_envs = app.project.config.internal_envs
78|        target_matrices = app.project.config.internal_matrices
79|    else:
80|        target_standalone_envs = app.project.config.envs
81|        target_matrices = app.project.config.matrices
82|
83|    for env_name in envs:
84|        if env_name not in target_standalone_envs and env_name not in target_matrices:
85|            app.abort(f"Environment `{env_name}` is not defined by project config")
86|
87|    env_names = set(envs)
88|
89|    matrix_columns: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {
90|        "Name": {},
91|        "Type": {},
92|        "Envs": {},
93|        "Features": {},
94|        "Dependencies": {},
95|        "Environment variables": {},
96|        "Scripts": {},
97|        "Description": {},
98|    }
99|    matrix_envs = set()
100|    for i, (matrix_name, matrix_data) in enumerate(target_matrices.items()):
101|        matrix_envs.update(matrix_data["envs"])
102|
103|        if env_names and matrix_name not in env_names:
104|            continue
105|
106|        config = matrix_data["config"]
107|        matrix_columns["Name"][i] = matrix_name
108|        matrix_columns["Type"][i] = config["type"]
109|        matrix_columns["Envs"][i] = "\n".join(matrix_data["envs"])
110|
111|        if config.get("features"):
112|            if app.project.metadata.hatch.metadata.allow_ambiguous_features:
113|                matrix_columns["Features"][i] = "\n".join(sorted(set(config["features"])))
114|            else:
115|                matrix_columns["Features"][i] = "\n".join(
116|                    sorted({normalize_project_name(f) for f in config["features"]})
117|                )
118|
119|        dependencies = []
120|        if config.get("dependencies"):
121|            dependencies.extend(config["dependencies"])
122|        if config.get("extra-dependencies"):
123|            dependencies.extend(config["extra-dependencies"])
124|        if dependencies:
125|            normalized_dependencies = set()
126|            for dependency in dependencies:
127|                try:
128|                    req = Dependency(dependency)
129|                except InvalidDependencyError:
130|                    normalized_dependencies.add(dependency)
131|                else:
132|                    normalized_dependencies.add(get_normalized_dependency(req))
133|
134|            matrix_columns["Dependencies"][i] = "\n".join(sorted(normalized_dependencies))
135|
136|        if config.get("env-vars"):
137|            matrix_columns["Environment variables"][i] = "\n".join(
138|                "=".join(item) for item in sorted(config["env-vars"].items())
139|            )
140|
141|        if config.get("scripts"):
142|            matrix_columns["Scripts"][i] = "\n".join(
143|                sorted(script for script in config["scripts"] if app.verbose or not script.startswith("_"))
144|            )
145|
146|        if config.get("description"):
147|            matrix_columns["Description"][i] = config["description"].strip()
148|
149|    standalone_columns: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {
150|        "Name": {},
151|        "Type": {},
152|        "Features": {},
153|        "Dependencies": {},
154|        "Environment variables": {},
155|        "Scripts": {},
156|        "Description": {},
157|    }
158|    standalone_envs = (
159|        (env_name, config)
160|        for env_name, config in target_standalone_envs.items()
161|        if env_names or env_name not in matrix_envs
162|    )
163|    for i, (env_name, config) in enumerate(standalone_envs):
164|        if env_names and env_name not in env_names:
165|            continue
166|
167|        environment = app.project.get_environment(env_name)
168|
169|        standalone_columns["Name"][i] = env_name
170|        standalone_columns["Type"][i] = config["type"]
171|
172|        if environment.features:
173|            standalone_columns["Features"][i] = "\n".join(environment.features)
174|
175|        if environment.environment_dependencies_complex:
176|            standalone_columns["Dependencies"][i] = "\n".join(
177|                sorted({get_normalized_dependency(d) for d in environment.environment_dependencies_complex})
178|            )
179|
180|        env_vars = dict(environment.env_vars)
181|        env_vars.pop(AppEnvVars.ENV_ACTIVE)
182|        if env_vars:
183|            standalone_columns["Environment variables"][i] = "\n".join(
184|                "=".join(item) for item in sorted(env_vars.items())
185|            )
186|
187|        if environment.scripts:
188|            standalone_columns["Scripts"][i] = "\n".join(
189|                sorted(script for script in environment.scripts if app.verbose or not script.startswith("_"))
190|            )
191|
192|        if environment.description:
193|            standalone_columns["Description"][i] = environment.description.strip()
194|
195|    column_options = {}
196|    for title in matrix_columns:
197|        if title != "Description":
198|            column_options[title] = {"no_wrap": True}
199|
200|    app.display_table(
201|        "" if hide_titles else "Standalone",
202|        standalone_columns,
203|        show_lines=True,
204|        column_options=column_options,
205|        force_ascii=force_ascii,
206|    )
207|    app.display_table(
208|        "" if hide_titles else "Matrices",
209|        matrix_columns,
210|        show_lines=True,
211|        column_options=column_options,
212|        force_ascii=force_ascii,
213|    )

4|import sys
5|from importlib.metadata import Distribution, DistributionFinder
6|from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
7|
8|from packaging.markers import default_environment

10|from hatch.dep.core import Dependency
11|from hatch.utils.fs import Path
12|
13|if TYPE_CHECKING:
14|    from collections.abc import Sequence
15|
16|
17|class InstalledDistributions:
18|    def __init__(self, *, sys_path: list[str] | None = None, environment: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
19|        self.__sys_path: list[str] = sys.path if sys_path is None else sys_path
20|        self.__environment: dict[str, str] = (
21|            default_environment() if environment is None else environment  # type: ignore[assignment]
22|        )
23|        self.__resolver = Distribution.discover(context=DistributionFinder.Context(path=self.__sys_path))
24|        self.__distributions: dict[str, Distribution] = {}
25|        self.__search_exhausted = False
26|        self.__canonical_regex = re.compile(r"[-_.]+")
27|
28|    def dependencies_in_sync(self, dependencies: list[Dependency]) -> bool:
29|        return all(self.dependency_in_sync(dependency) for dependency in dependencies)
30|
31|    def missing_dependencies(self, dependencies: Sequence[Dependency]) -> list[Dependency]:
32|        return [dependency for dependency in dependencies if not self.dependency_in_sync(dependency)]
33|
34|    def dependency_in_sync(self, dependency: Dependency, *, environment: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> bool:
35|        if environment is None:
36|            environment = self.__environment
37|
38|        if dependency.marker and not dependency.marker.evaluate(environment):
39|            return True
40|
41|        distribution = self[dependency.name]
42|        if distribution is None:
43|            return False
44|
45|        extras = dependency.extras
46|        if extras:
47|            transitive_dependencies: list[str] = distribution.metadata.get_all("Requires-Dist", [])
48|            if not transitive_dependencies:
49|                return False
50|
51|            available_extras: list[str] = distribution.metadata.get_all("Provides-Extra", [])
52|
53|            for dependency_string in transitive_dependencies:
54|                transitive_dependency = Dependency(dependency_string)
55|                if not transitive_dependency.marker:
56|                    continue
57|
58|                for extra in extras:
59|                    # FIXME: This may cause a build to never be ready if newer versions do not provide the desired
60|                    # extra and it's just a user error/typo. See: https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7122
61|                    if extra not in available_extras:
62|                        return False
63|
64|                    extra_environment = dict(environment)
65|                    extra_environment["extra"] = extra
66|                    if not self.dependency_in_sync(transitive_dependency, environment=extra_environment):
67|                        return False
68|
69|        if dependency.specifier and not dependency.specifier.contains(distribution.version):
70|            return False
71|
72|        # TODO: handle https://discuss.python.org/t/11938
73|        if dependency.url:
74|            direct_url_file = distribution.read_text("direct_url.json")
75|            if direct_url_file is None:
76|                return False
77|
78|            import json
79|
80|            # https://packaging.python.org/specifications/direct-url/
81|            direct_url_data = json.loads(direct_url_file)
82|            url = direct_url_data["url"]
83|            if "dir_info" in direct_url_data:
84|                dir_info = direct_url_data["dir_info"]
85|                editable = dir_info.get("editable", False)
86|                if editable != dependency.editable:
87|                    return False
88|
89|                if Path.from_uri(url) != dependency.path:
90|                    return False
91|
92|                if direct_url_data.get("subdirectory") != dependency.subdirectory:
93|                    return False
94|
95|            if "vcs_info" in direct_url_data:
96|                vcs_info = direct_url_data["vcs_info"]
97|                vcs = vcs_info["vcs"]
98|                commit_id = vcs_info["commit_id"]
99|                requested_revision = vcs_info.get("requested_revision")
100|
101|                # Try a few variations, see https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#direct-references
102|                if (
103|                    requested_revision and dependency.url == f"{vcs}+{url}@{requested_revision}#{commit_id}"
104|                ) or dependency.url == f"{vcs}+{url}@{commit_id}":
105|                    return True
106|
107|                if dependency.url in {f"{vcs}+{url}", f"{vcs}+{url}@{requested_revision}"}:
108|                    import subprocess
109|
110|                    if vcs == "git":
111|                        vcs_cmd = [vcs, "ls-remote", url]
112|                        if requested_revision:
113|                            vcs_cmd.append(requested_revision)
114|                    # TODO: add elifs for hg, svn, and bzr https://github.com/pypa/hatch/issues/760
115|                    else:
116|                        return False
117|                    result = subprocess.run(vcs_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)  # noqa: PLW1510
118|                    if result.returncode or not result.stdout.strip():
119|                        return False
120|                    latest_commit_id, *_ = result.stdout.split()
121|                    return commit_id == latest_commit_id
122|
123|                return False
124|
125|        return True
126|
127|    def __getitem__(self, item: str) -> Distribution | None:
128|        item = self.__canonical_regex.sub("-", item).lower()
129|        possible_distribution = self.__distributions.get(item)
130|        if possible_distribution is not None:
131|            return possible_distribution
132|
133|        if self.__search_exhausted:
134|            return None
135|
136|        for distribution in self.__resolver:
137|            name = distribution.metadata["Name"]
138|            if name is None:
139|                continue
140|
141|            name = self.__canonical_regex.sub("-", name).lower()
142|            self.__distributions[name] = distribution
143|            if name == item:
144|                return distribution
145|
146|        self.__search_exhausted = True
147|
148|        return None
149|
150|
151|def dependencies_in_sync(
152|    dependencies: list[Dependency], sys_path: list[str] | None = None, environment: dict[str, str] | None = None
153|) -> bool:  # no cov
154|    # This function is unused and only temporarily exists for plugin backwards compatibility.
155|    distributions = InstalledDistributions(sys_path=sys_path, environment=environment)
156|    return distributions.dependencies_in_sync(dependencies)

10|
11|# Hatch v1.8.0
12|
13|Hatch [v1.8.0](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/releases/tag/hatch-v1.8.0) brings Python distribution management, static analysis and formatting backed by Ruff, and binaries for every platform.
14|
15|<!-- more -->
16|
17|## Installation made easy
18|
19|One thing that has been a perpetual problem for Hatch and other Python applications is that Python itself is a dependency. You, and more importantly your users, need to in some way get Python before your software can even be used. The recommended way to go about that is platform-dependent and even differs based on your target audience. I viewed this as a central UX problem for Hatch and so severe that I took a bit of a hiatus to solve it.
20|
21|Luckily, I have to my satisfaction solved this problem in the form of [PyApp](https://github.com/ofek/pyapp). It is a runtime installer for Python projects written in Rust. Apps are distributed as standalone executables as users have come to expect and bootstrapping occurs upon the first invocation. Here is an example of what you would see the first time you run a binary from this release:
22|
23|<figure markdown>
24|  ![Installation example](release-hatch-180/install-demo.gif){ loading=lazy role="img" }
25|</figure>
26|
27|Now that we have binaries, creating installers for different platforms becomes trivial. Starting with this release not only are binaries available for every platform but also we have installers for Windows and macOS. The installer for macOS is signed using a certificate from the same account used to sign the official distributions from https://www.python.org, so users will not get any security pop-ups. Shout out to @ewdurbin for their extreme generosity in setting up multiple certificates in their free time!
28|
29|These installers and binaries are now the [recommended way](../../install.md) to install and update Hatch. These binaries have built-in management so you can update to the latest version by running `hatch self update`.
30|
31|!!! note "Windows signing"
32|    In future we will sign the installers for Windows but I did not have time to look into how that works. macOS signing took way longer than I anticipated :sweat_smile:
33|
34|## Python management
35|
36|For a long time I and other users have desired that Hatch gain the ability to manage Python distributions. In my mind this was always blocked on a better installation experience because there was sort of a chicken-or-egg problem where you want a Python manager but you first need Python. No longer is that the case!
37|
38|The new [`python`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-python) command group allows for easy installation of various distributions to arbitrary locations which are then added to your PATH by default. Hatch supports CPython and PyPy distributions:
39|
40|<figure markdown>
41|  ![Available Python distributions](release-hatch-180/available-pythons.png){ loading=lazy width="200" role="img" }
42|</figure>
43|
44|## Virtual environment Python resolution
45|
46|The `virtual` environment type is now far more intelligent when resolving the parent distribution to use and guarantees that, when no specific version is requested, the resolved distribution will always be [compatible](../../config/metadata.md#python-support) with the project.
47|
48|Additionally, when a requested version cannot be found on PATH it will [automatically](../../plugins/environment/virtual.md#python-resolution) be downloaded and managed internally.
49|
50|## Static analysis
51|
52|There is a new [`fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-fmt) command, backed entirely by [Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff), that checks and fixes your code for formatting and linting issues.
53|
54|Starting with this release, Hatch maintains [default settings](../../config/internal/static-analysis.md#default-settings) that are guaranteed to be up-to-date and represent best practices for programming in modern Python. The idea is to provide defaults that are so broadly applicable that the majority of users will maintain little if any of their own [overrides](../../config/internal/static-analysis.md#extending-config).
55|
56|The default behavior is internal management of settings to provide an OOTB experience that works. It is recommended however that you [persist](../../config/internal/static-analysis.md#persistent-config) the default config file in version control so that other tools like IDEs can utilize your full configuration.
57|
58|Since Ruff is now provided as a built-in feature, new project templates no longer have such configuration and are much less verbose.
59|
60|## Build improvements
61|
62|[Building](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-build) projects that do not use Hatchling as a backend is now supported and such builds are managed with the standard [build](https://github.com/pypa/build) tool.
63|
64|The bridge between Hatch and the Hatchling CLI has been removed. Previously, the builder would send serialized messages to Hatch that would contain the desired content and style for each line of output. This was done in an effort to allow builder and build hook plugins to output pretty messages without actually requiring a dependency like [Rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich). A problem that arises with this is that builders that invoke subprocesses will not display ANSI codes as one might expect and will lose out on the interactive experience of such invocations, like the built-in [binary builder plugin](../../plugins/builder/binary.md) calling `cargo build`. So now everything is simpler at the expense of no colored output without manual logic, or adding a dependency if you're a third-party plugin.
65|
66|## Faster environment usage
67|
68|[Spawning a shell](../../environment.md#entering-environments) or [running commands](../../environment.md#command-execution) within environments always first checks that your project's dependencies are satisfied and if not synchronizes the environment with what is defined. Previously, this had the potential to be quite slow for projects that have many dependencies.
69|
70|Now the set of dependency definitions is [hashed](../../plugins/environment/reference.md#hatch.env.plugin.interface.EnvironmentInterface.dependency_hash) and no check is performed if the hash is the same as before, significantly speeding up environment usage in most cases.
71|
72|## Hatchling
73|
74|Hatch now depends on Hatchling [v1.19.0](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/releases/tag/hatchling-v1.19.0), which was also just released.
75|
76|### Better defaults
77|
78|Hatchling is all about providing the best possible defaults, even at the expense of backward compatibility. In this release, there are two breaking changes that provide a much better user experience and were in fact requested by users.
79|
80|- Both the [`force-include`](../../config/build.md#forced-inclusion) option and the [`force_include_editable`](../../plugins/builder/wheel.md#build-data) wheel build data setting now raise errors if source paths do not exist.
81|- The `wheel` build target now raises an error when no file inclusion options have been defined and none of its [heuristics](../../plugins/builder/wheel.md#default-file-selection) to determine what to ship are satisfied.
82|
83|### Binary build target
84|
85|A new [`binary`](../../plugins/builder/binary.md) build target is now stable that allows for the building of standalone binaries for projects. This is what Hatch itself uses for its binaries.
86|
87|## Meta
88|
89|### Why Hatch?
90|
91|A [new page](../../why.md) has been introduced that discusses the value proposition of Hatch and Hatchling in comparison to alternatives. Currently, it only addresses a few features but in future this page will become more comprehensive.
92|
93|### Future
94|
95|Upcoming features include a `test` command, commands to manage dependencies, and workspaces functionality [similar to Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch14-03-cargo-workspaces.html) that will make managing monorepos far easier.
96|
97|Next year there will be two large efforts that you should expect to see:
98|
99|1. A significant amount of my free time (and some at work) will be devoted to introducing lock file functionality in Hatch and trying to get whatever that happens to be standardized.
100|
101|    I met with @brettcannon about his thoughts post-[PEP 665](https://peps.python.org/pep-0665/) and about [mousebender](https://github.com/brettcannon/mousebender). I also met with the [prefix.dev](https://github.com/prefix-dev) team about [rip](https://github.com/prefix-dev/rip) and was fortunate enough to be shown a demo before its official announcement.
102|
103|    At the moment, the two options I see are to either go all in and contribute to mousebender or rely on the Prefix folks and use rip. The latter has the benefit of _potentially_ supporting Conda as a side effect with the downside of being quite new with the spec firmly out of our control. The former has the benefit of being able to easily gain institutional support from the Python packaging team and each of our employers with the downside being a significant amount of work needing to be done.
104|
105|1. When @henryiii is able to get some free time away from teaching I plan to work with him once again and push very hard for the Python build ecosystem to adopt the [extensionlib](https://github.com/ofek/extensionlib) approach.
106|
107|    I am of the opinion that the Python community has not fully completed the expressed outcome of [PEP 517][] in that build backends are still (for the most part) reliant on setuptools for building non-Python code bases.
108|
109|    Basically, there are components that interact with compilers to produce extension modules and components that pack files into an archive which we call a build backend. These are two distinct pieces of functionality and my view is that there should be an API that allows backends to consume extension module builders to find out where things got created and where they should be shipped inside archives.
110|
111|    In this hypothetical future any build backend would be able to trigger the building of extension modules based on user configuration.
112|
113|### Support
114|
115|If you or your organization finds value in what Hatch provides, consider a [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/ofek) to assist with maintenance and more rapid development!

66|        credentials = AuthenticationCredentials(

69|            options=options,
70|            repo=repo,
71|            repo_config=repo_config,
72|        )
73|
74|        index = PackageIndex(
75|            repo_config["url"],
76|            user=credentials.username,
77|            auth=credentials.password,
78|            ca_cert=options.get("ca_cert", repo_config.get("ca-cert")),
79|            client_cert=options.get("client_cert", repo_config.get("client-cert")),
80|            client_key=options.get("client_key", repo_config.get("client-key")),
81|        )
82|
83|        existing_artifacts: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
84|

102|

109|

114|                    response.raise_for_status()
115|                except Exception:  # no cov  # noqa: BLE001
116|                    existing_artifacts[project_name] = set()
117|                else:

119|
120|            if artifact.name in existing_artifacts[project_name]:
121|                self.app.display_warning("already exists")
122|                continue
123|
124|            try:

126|            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
127|                self.app.display_error("failed")

129|            else:

150|def recurse_artifacts(artifacts: list, root) -> Iterable[Path]:
151|    for raw_artifact in artifacts:
152|        artifact = Path(raw_artifact)
153|        if not artifact.is_absolute():
154|            artifact = root / artifact
155|
156|        if artifact.is_file():

158|        elif artifact.is_dir():

--- FILE: docs/why.md ---
1|# Why Hatch?
2|
3|-----
4|
5|The high level value proposition of Hatch is that if one adopts all functionality then many other tools become unnecessary since there is support for everything one might require. Further, if one chooses to use only specific features then there are still benefits compared to alternatives.
6|
7|## Build backend
8|
9|Hatchling, the [build backend](config/build.md#build-system) sister project, has many benefits compared to [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools). Here we only compare setuptools as that is the one most people are familiar with.
10|
11|- **Better defaults:** The default behavior for setuptools is often not desirable for the average user.
12|    - For source distributions, setuptools has a custom enumeration of files that get included and excluded by default. Hatchling takes the [defaults](plugins/builder/sdist.md#default-file-selection) from your version control system such as Git's `.gitignore` file.
13|    - For wheels, setuptools attempts to find every directory that looks like a Python package. This is often undesirable as you might ship files to the end-user unintentionally such as test or tooling directories. Hatchling [defaults](plugins/builder/wheel.md#default-file-selection) to very specific inclusion based on the project name and errors if no heuristic is satisfied.
14|- **Ease of configurability:** Hatchling was designed based on a history of significant challenges when configuring setuptools.
15|    - Hatchling [uses](config/build.md#patterns) the same glob pattern syntax as Git itself for every option which is what most users are familiar with. On the other hand, setuptools uses shell-style glob patterns for source distributions while wheels use a mix of shell-style globs and Python package syntax.
16|    - Configuring what gets included in source distributions requires a separate [`MANIFEST.in` file](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/miscellaneous.html#using-manifest-in). The custom syntax and directives must be learned and it is difficult knowing which options in the main files like `setup.py` influence the behavior and under what conditions. For Hatchling, everything gets [configured](config/build.md) in a single file under dedicated sections for specific targets like `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]`.
17|    - By default, non-Python files are excluded from wheels. Including such files requires usually verbose rules for every nested package directory. Hatchling makes no such distinction between file types and acts more like a general build system one might already be familiar with.
18|- **Editable installations:** The default behavior of Hatchling allows for proper static analysis by external tools such as IDEs. With setuptools, you must provide [additional configuration](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/development_mode.html#legacy-behavior) which means that by default, for example, you would not get autocompletion in Visual Studio Code. This is marked as a legacy feature and may in fact be removed in future versions of setuptools.
19|- **Reproducibility:** Hatchling builds reproducible wheels and source distributions by default. setuptools [does not support this](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/2133) for source distributions and there is no guarantee that wheels are reproducible.
20|- **Extensibility:** Although it is possible to [extend](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/extension.html) setuptools, the API is quite low level. Hatchling has the concept of [plugins](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/plugins/about/) that are separated into discrete types and only expose what is necessary, leading to an easier developer experience.
21|
22|***Why not?:***
23|
24|If building extension modules is required then it is recommended that you continue using setuptools, or even other backends that specialize in interfacing with compilers.
25|
26|## Environment management
27|
28|Here we compare to both `tox` and `nox`. At a high level, there are a few common advantages:
29|
30|- **Python management:** Hatch is able to automatically download [Python distributions](plugins/environment/virtual.md#internal-distributions) on the fly when specific versions that environments request cannot be found. The alternatives will raise an error, with the option to ignore unknown distributions.
31|- **Philosophy:** In the alternatives, environments are for the most part treated as executable units where a dependency set is associated with an action. If you are familiar with container ecosystems, this would be like defining a `CMD` at the end of a Dockerfile but without the ability to change the action at runtime. This involves significant wasted disk space usually because one often requires slight modifications to the actions and therefore will define entirely different environments inherited from a base config just to perform different logic. Additionally, this can be confusing to users not just configuration-wise but also for execution of the different environments.
32|
33|    In Hatch, [environments](environment.md) are treated as isolated areas where you can execute arbitrary commands at runtime. For example, you can define a single test environment with named [scripts](config/environment/overview.md#scripts) that runs unit vs non-unit tests, each command being potentially very long but named however you wish so you get to control the interface. Since environments are treated as places where work is performed, you can also [spawn a shell](environment.md#entering-environments) into any which will execute a subprocess that automatically drops into your [shell of choice](config/hatch.md#shell). Your shell will be configured appropriately like `python` on PATH being updated and the prompt being changed to reflect the chosen environment.
34|
35|- **Configuration:**
36|    - `nox` config is defined in Python which often leads to increased verbosity and makes it challenging to onboard folks compared to a standardized format with known behaviors.
37|- **Extensibility:**
38|    - `tox` allows for [extending](https://tox.wiki/en/4.11.4/plugins_api.html) most aspects of its functionality however the API is so low-level and attached to internals that creating plugins may be challenging. For example, [here](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/4f4cf10613797e97e7155c75859532a0732d1dff/datadog_checks_dev/datadog_checks/dev/plugin/tox.py) is a `tox` plugin that was [migrated](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/4eb2a1d530bcf810542cf9e45b48fadc7057301c/datadog_checks_dev/datadog_checks/dev/plugin/hatch/environment_collector.py#L100-L148) to an equivalent Hatch [environment collector plugin](plugins/environment-collector/reference.md).
39|    - `nox` is configured with Python so for the local project you can do whatever you want, however there is no concept of third-party plugins per se. To achieve that, you must usually use a package that wraps `nox` and use that package's imports instead ([example](https://github.com/cjolowicz/nox-poetry)).
40|
41|***Why not?:***
42|
43|If you are using `nox` and you wish to migrate, and for some reason you [notify](https://nox.thea.codes/en/stable/config.html#nox.sessions.Session.notify) sessions, then migration wouldn't be a straight translation but rather you might have to redesign that conditional step.
44|
45|## Python management
46|
47|Here we compare [Python management](tutorials/python/manage.md) to that of [pyenv](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv).
48|
49|- ***Cross-platform:*** Hatch allows for the same experience no matter the system whereas `pyenv` does not support Windows so you must use an [entirely different project](https://github.com/pyenv-win/pyenv-win) that tries to emulate the functionality.
50|- ***No build dependencies:*** Hatch guarantees that every [available distribution](cli/reference.md#hatch-python-show) is prebuilt whereas the alternative requires one to maintain a precise [build environment](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv/wiki#suggested-build-environment) which differs by platform and potentially Python version. Another benefit to this is extremely fast installations since the distributions are simply downloaded and unpacked.
51|- ***Optimized by default:*** The [CPython distributions](plugins/environment/virtual.md#cpython) are built with profile guided optimization and link-time optimization, resulting in a 10-30% performance improvement depending on the workload. These distributions have seen wide adoption throughout the industry and are even used by the build system [Bazel](https://bazel.build).
52|- ***Simplicity:*** Hatch treats Python installations as just another directory that one would add to PATH. It can do this for you or you can manage PATH yourself, even allowing for custom install locations. On the other hand, `pyenv` operates by adding [shims](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv/tree/74a2523c97d2e5c1dbdca7b58f3372324ccad4e6#understanding-shims) which then act as wrappers around the actual underlying binaries. This has many unfortunate side effects:
53|    - It is incumbent upon the user to manage which specific Python comes first via the CLI, switch when necessary, and/or have a mental model of which versions are exposed globally and locally per-project. This can become confusing quite quickly. When working with Hatch, your global Python installations are only important insofar as they are on PATH somewhere since environments do not use them directly but rather create virtual environments from them, always using a version that is compatible with your project.
54|    - Configuration is required for each shell to properly set up `pyenv` on start, leading to inconsistencies when running processes that do not spawn a shell.
55|    - Debugging issues with Python search paths can be extremely difficult, especially for users of software. If you or users have ever ran into an issue where code was being executed that you did not anticipate, the issue is almost always `pyenv` influencing the `python` on PATH.
56|
57|***Why not?:***
58|
59|Currently, Hatch does not allow for the installation of specific patch release versions but rather only uses minor release granularity that tracks the latest patch release. If specific patch releases are important to you then it is best to use an alternative installation mechanism.

1|# Hatch configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|Configuration for Hatch itself is stored in a `config.toml` file located by default in one of the following platform-specific directories.
6|
7|| Platform | Path |
8|| --- | --- |
9|| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/hatch` |
10|| Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\hatch` |
11|| Unix | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hatch` (the [XDG_CONFIG_HOME](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html#variables) environment variable default is `~/.config`) |
12|
13|You can select a custom path to the file using the `--config` [root option](../cli/reference.md#hatch) or by setting the `HATCH_CONFIG` environment variable.
14|
15|The file can be managed by the [`config`](../cli/reference.md#hatch-config) command group.
16|
17|## Mode
18|
19|The `mode` key controls how Hatch selects the project to work on.
20|
21|### Local
22|
23|```toml tab="config.toml"
24|mode = "local"
25|```
26|
27|By default, Hatch will look for a `pyproject.toml` file in the current working directory
28|and any parent directories. The directory storing the first found file will be considered the project root.
29|
30|### Project
31|
32|```toml tab="config.toml"
33|mode = "project"
34|project = "proj1"
35|
36|[projects]
37|proj1 = "/path/to/project1"
38|proj2 = {"location": "/path/to/project2"}
39|
40|[dirs]
41|project = ["/path/to/monorepo1", "/path/to/monorepo2"]
42|```
43|
44|In this mode, Hatch will only work on the selected `project`. The project is located using multiple heuristics:
45|
46|1. If the project is defined in the `projects` table then it must be a string, or an inline table with a `location` key, that is the full path to the project.
47|2. If the project matches a subdirectory in any of the directories listed in `dirs.project`, then that will be used as the project root.
48|
49|An error will occur if the project cannot be found.
50|
51|You can use the [`config set`](../cli/reference.md#hatch-config-set) command to change the project you are working on:
52|
53|```console
54|$ hatch config set project proj2
55|New setting:
56|project = "proj2"
57|```
58|
59|The project can be selected on a per-command basis with the `-p`/`--project` (environment variable `HATCH_PROJECT`) [root option](../cli/reference.md#hatch).
60|
61|### Aware
62|
63|```toml tab="config.toml"
64|mode = "aware"
65|```
66|
67|This is essentially the `local` mode with a fallback to the `project` mode.
68|
69|## Shell
70|
71|You can control the shell used to [enter environments](../environment.md#entering-environments) with the `shell` key.
72|
73|If defined as a string, it must be the name of one of the [supported shells](#supported) and be available along your `PATH`.
74|
75|```toml tab="config.toml"
76|shell = "fish"
77|```
78|
79|If the executable name of your shell differs from the supported name, you can define the `shell` as a table with `name` and `path` keys.
80|
81|```toml tab="config.toml"
82|[shell]
83|name = "bash"
84|path = "/bin/ash"
85|```
86|
87|You can change the default arguments used to spawn most shells with the `args` key. The default for such supported shells is usually `["-i"]`.
88|
89|```toml tab="config.toml"
90|[shell]
91|name = "bash"
92|args = ["--login"]
93|```
94|
95|### Supported
96|
97|| Shell | Name | Arguments | macOS | Windows | Unix |
98|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
99|| [Almquist shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almquist_shell) | `ash` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | | :white_check_mark: |
100|| [Bash](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/) | `bash` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
101|| [Command Prompt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cmd.exe) | `cmd` | | | :white_check_mark: | |
102|| [C shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_shell) | `csh` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | | :white_check_mark: |
103|| [fish](https://github.com/fish-shell/fish-shell) | `fish` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | | :white_check_mark: |
104|| [Nushell](https://github.com/nushell/nushell) | `nu` | `[]` | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
105|| [PowerShell](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell) | `pwsh`, `powershell` | | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
106|| [tcsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tcsh) | `tcsh` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | | :white_check_mark: |
107|| [xonsh](https://github.com/xonsh/xonsh) | `xonsh` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
108|| [Z shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z_shell) | `zsh` | `["-i"]` | :white_check_mark: | | :white_check_mark: |
109|
110|### Default
111|
112|Hatch will attempt to use the current shell based on parent processes. If the shell cannot be determined, then on Windows systems Hatch will use the `SHELL` environment variable, if present, followed by the `COMSPEC` environment variable, defaulting to `cmd`. On all other platforms only the `SHELL` environment variable will be used, defaulting to `bash`.
113|
114|## Directories
115|
116|### Data
117|
118|```toml tab="config.toml"
119|[dirs]
120|data = "..."
121|```
122|
123|This is the directory that is used to persist data. By default it is set to one of the following platform-specific directories.
124|
125|| Platform | Path |
126|| --- | --- |
127|| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/hatch` |
128|| Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\hatch` |
129|| Unix | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hatch` (the [XDG_DATA_HOME](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html#variables) environment variable default is `~/.local/share`) |
130|
131|You can select a custom path to the directory using the `--data-dir` [root option](../cli/reference.md#hatch) or by setting the `HATCH_DATA_DIR` environment variable.
132|
133|### Cache
134|
135|```toml tab="config.toml"
136|[dirs]
137|cache = "..."
138|```
139|
140|This is the directory that is used to cache data. By default it is set to one of the following platform-specific directories.
141|
142|| Platform | Path |
143|| --- | --- |
144|| macOS | `~/Library/Caches/hatch` |
145|| Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\hatch\Cache` |
146|| Unix | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/hatch` (the [XDG_CACHE_HOME](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html#variables) environment variable default is `~/.cache`) |
147|
148|You can select a custom path to the directory using the `--cache-dir` [root option](../cli/reference.md#hatch) or by setting the `HATCH_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.
149|
150|### Environments
151|
152|```toml tab="config.toml"
153|[dirs.env]
154|<ENV_TYPE> = "..."
155|```
156|
157|This determines where to store environments, with every key being the [type of environment](environment/overview.md#type) and the value being the desired storage location.
158|
159|For example, if you wanted to store [virtual environments](../plugins/environment/virtual.md) in a `.virtualenvs` directory within your home directory, you could specify the following:
160|
161|```toml tab="config.toml"
162|[dirs.env]
163|virtual = "~/.virtualenvs"
164|```
165|
166|Any environment variables are also expanded.
167|
168|If the path is not absolute, then it will be relative to the project root. So if you wanted to use a directory named `.hatch` in each project directory, you could do:
169|
170|```toml tab="config.toml"
171|[dirs.env]
172|virtual = ".hatch"
173|```
174|
175|Any type of environment that is not explicitly defined will default to `<DATA_DIR>/env/<ENV_TYPE>`.
176|
177|### Python installations
178|
179|```toml tab="config.toml"
180|[dirs]
181|python = "..."
182|```
183|
184|This determines where to install specific versions of Python.
185|
186|The following values have special meanings:
187|
188|| Value | Path |
189|| --- | --- |
190|| `isolated` (default) | `<DATA_DIR>/pythons` |
191|
192|## Terminal
193|
194|You can configure how all output is displayed using the `terminal.styles` table. These settings are also applied to all plugins.
195|
196|```toml tab="config.toml"
197|[terminal.styles]
198|error = "..."
199|...
200|```
201|
202|Cross-platform terminal capabilities are provided by [Rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich).
203|
204|### Output levels
205|
206|The levels of output are as follows. Note that the [verbosity](../cli/about.md) indicates the minimum level at which the output is displayed.
207|
208|| Level | Default | Verbosity | Description |
209|| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
210|| `debug` | `bold` | 1 - 3 | Messages that are not useful for most user experiences |
211|| `error` | `bold red` | -2 | Messages indicating some unrecoverable error |
212|| `info` | `bold` | 0 | Messages conveying basic information |
213|| `success` | `bold cyan` | 0 | Messages indicating some positive outcome |
214|| `waiting` | `bold magenta` | 0 | Messages shown before potentially time consuming operations |
215|| `warning` | `bold yellow` | -1 | Messages conveying important information |
216|
217|See the [documentation](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/style.html) and [color reference](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/appendix/colors.html) for guidance on valid values.
218|
219|### Spinner
220|
221|You can select the [sequence](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/rich/_spinners.py) used for waiting animations with the `spinner` option.
222|
223|```toml tab="config.toml"
224|[terminal.styles]
225|spinner = "..."
226|```

9|
10|# Hatch v1.18.0
11|
12|Hatch [v1.18.0](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/releases/tag/hatch-v1.18.0) introduces dependency sources for redirecting packages at install time, a `--all` flag for building every workspace member at once, and a healthy batch of bug fixes.
13|
14|<!-- more -->
15|
16|## Dependency sources
17|
18|The new [`sources`](../../config/environment/sources.md) table redirects a dependency to somewhere other than the index it would normally come from — a local checkout, a Git branch, a URL, a private index, or another workspace member — **without touching the metadata you publish**.
19|
20|This is the workflow it is built for: you are developing against an unreleased fix in a library you depend on, and you want your environment to use your local clone while the wheel you ship keeps pointing at the released version.
21|
22|```toml config-example
23|[project]
24|dependencies = ["foo"]
25|
26|[tool.hatch.sources]
27|foo = "./packages/foo"
28|```
29|
30|The top-level `[tool.hatch.sources]` table is an alias for the `default` environment, so the example above is shorthand for `[tool.hatch.envs.default.sources]`.
31|
32|Sources are matched to your dependencies by name after [PEP 503](https://peps.python.org/pep-0503/#normalized-names) normalization, and both project dependencies and environment dependencies are eligible.
33|
34|### Every kind of origin
35|
36|```toml config-example
37|[tool.hatch.sources]
38|# A local project directory, editable by default
39|core = "./packages/core"
40|# A non-editable install from a subdirectory
41|utils = { path = "./monorepo", subdirectory = "packages/utils", editable = false }
42|# A Git branch, tag, or revision
43|client = { git = "https://github.com/example/client", branch = "main" }
44|# An archive
45|legacy = { url = "https://files.example.com/legacy-1.0.tar.gz" }
46|# A private index, passed to the installer as --extra-index-url
47|internal = { index = "https://pypi.example.com/simple" }
48|# A workspace member, resolved through workspace.members
49|my-pkg = { workspace = true }
50|```
51|
52|The `workspace = true` form is worth calling out: it lets you declare membership once in `workspace.members` and reference it from as many environments as you like, rather than repeating paths.
53|
54|### Inheritance
55|
56|Sources merge entry by entry, so an environment can override a single redirection while everything else it inherits stays put:
57|
58|```toml config-example
59|[tool.hatch.sources]
60|foo = "./packages/foo"
61|bar = "./packages/bar"
62|
63|[tool.hatch.envs.test-upstream.sources]
64|foo = { git = "https://github.com/example/foo", branch = "main" }
65|```
66|
67|Every environment here installs both packages from local checkouts, except `test-upstream`, which keeps the local `bar` but tracks upstream `foo`.
68|
69|### Checking your work
70|
71|Redirections that quietly do nothing are the failure mode worth guarding against, so [`hatch dep show sources`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-show) reports what each source targets and which dependencies of the active environment it actually redirects. A source matching no dependency is reported with a warning — which is usually how you find out you typed `httpx2` where you meant `httpx`.
72|
73|To prove your published metadata still resolves on its own, set `HATCH_NO_SOURCES` to disable every redirection:
74|
75|```
76|HATCH_NO_SOURCES=1 hatch env create
77|```
78|
79|That is a good thing to put in CI.
80|
81|A few deliberate boundaries: a dependency that already uses a [direct reference](../../config/dependency.md#direct-references) wins over a configured source, sources never apply to build requirements so that builds stay reproducible, and they do not influence the metadata of wheels produced by `hatch build`.
82|
83|## Building every workspace member
84|
85|[Workspaces](../../how-to/environment/workspace.md) arrived in v1.16.0, but releasing one still meant walking the members yourself. The [`build`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-build) command now takes `--all`/`-a`:
86|
87|```
88|hatch build --all
89|```
90|
91|This builds an sdist and a wheel for the workspace root and for every member of the selected environment, consolidating the artifacts in the root's `dist` directory — ready to hand straight to `twine upload dist/*`. Pass a location to put them elsewhere:
92|
93|```
94|hatch build --all out/artifacts
95|```
96|
97|The root is built first and does not need to list itself as a member. If your top-level `pyproject.toml` has no `project` table and exists purely to hold workspace configuration, the root is skipped and only the members are built.
98|
99|## Fixes
100|
101|This release carries a larger-than-usual batch of fixes.
102|
103|**`hatch run` responds to Ctrl-C again.** Commands run through `hatch run` had become uninterruptible: the parent process ignored `SIGINT`, and the child inherited that. Interrupting a long test run works as it should now.
104|
105|**Free-threaded builds get free-threaded interpreters.** When Hatch itself runs on a free-threaded build and has to install a Python distribution, it was selecting a GIL-enabled one — silently changing the execution model of the environment it just created. It now selects the distribution matching the running interpreter, such as `3.14t`. The new selectors described below also reach environment configuration: `python = "3.14t"` was initially rejected there even though `hatch python install 3.14t` accepted it, and both paths now agree.
106|
107|**Prereleases are never selected automatically.** With Python 3.15 distributions now available (currently 3.15.0rc1), the fallback that picks the latest compatible version could have handed you a release candidate without asking. Automatic selection is restricted to stable releases; a prerelease still installs when you request one explicitly.
108|
109|**Type checking works on Windows.** The Pyrefly configuration Hatch generates for `hatch check types` embedded absolute paths containing backslashes, which TOML read as escape sequences, producing an invalid config.
110|
111|**Environment creation survives uninstalled metadata hooks.** Creating an environment crashed when the project configured a metadata hook that was not installed in the Hatch CLI's own environment.
112|
113|**Coverage data no longer leaks between runs.** `hatch test --cover` now erases stale coverage data before running, so results reflect the run in front of you.
114|
115|**No more hardcoded reliance on `pip`.** Internal dependency installation now goes through `uv`.
116|
117|## Also in this release
118|
119|- `tool.hatch.requires-hatch` — a version specifier set that commands reading your project's metadata enforce against the running version of Hatch, so a project that depends on newer behavior can say so. See [how to constrain Hatch](../../how-to/config/constrain-hatch.md).
120|- `hatch version` can now bump a version that is statically defined by `project.version`, rewriting `pyproject.toml` in place instead of refusing. Pass `--force` to allow an explicit downgrade.
121|- Free-threaded distribution names such as `3.13t` and `3.14t` are first-class in the `python` commands and the environment `python` option, rather than requiring `HATCH_PYTHON_VARIANT_GIL`.
122|- Python 3.15 distributions are available to install, and the default CPython distributions have been upgraded to the 20260807 release.
123|
124|### Support
125|
126|If you or your organization finds value in what Hatch provides, consider sponsoring our maintainers [Ofek](https://github.com/sponsors/ofek) and [Cary](https://github.com/sponsors/cjames23) to assist with maintenance and more rapid development!

100|    *,

102|) -> list[str]:
103|    """Expand extras on local-project dependencies transitively.
104|
105|    Parameters
106|    ----------
107|    deps:
108|        Raw PEP 508 dependency strings to resolve.
109|    local_projects:
110|        Mapping of normalized project name → raw optional-dependencies dict.
111|        Self-referencing extras within each project AND cross-project extras
112|        are expanded in a single BFS pass.
113|    warn:
114|        Warning callback for undefined extras.
115|
116|    Returns only dependency strings that do not reference any local project.
117|    """
118|    from collections import deque
119|
120|    from packaging.requirements import Requirement
121|
122|    from hatchling.metadata.utils import normalize_project_name
123|
124|    external: list[str] = []
125|    seen: set[str] = set()
126|    queue: deque[str] = deque(deps)
127|
128|    # Pre-build normalized lookups for each project's optional-deps keys.
129|    normalized_lookups: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
130|    for project_name, optional_deps in local_projects.items():
131|        lookup: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
132|        for key, value in optional_deps.items():
133|            lookup[key] = value
134|            norm_key = normalize_project_name(key)
135|            if norm_key != key:
136|                lookup.setdefault(norm_key, value)
137|        normalized_lookups[project_name] = lookup
138|
139|    while queue:
140|        dep_str = queue.popleft()
141|        if dep_str in seen:
142|            continue
143|        seen.add(dep_str)
144|
145|        req = Requirement(dep_str)
146|        name = normalize_project_name(req.name)
147|
148|        if name not in local_projects:
149|            external.append(dep_str)
150|            continue
151|
152|        if not req.extras:
153|            continue
154|
155|        lookup = normalized_lookups[name]
156|        for extra in req.extras:
157|            norm_extra = normalize_project_name(extra)
158|            extra_deps = lookup.get(extra) or lookup.get(norm_extra)
159|            if extra_deps is None:

163|                        f"`{extra}`, which local project `{name}` does not define"
164|                    )
165|            else:

1|# Virtual environment
2|
3|-----
4|
5|This uses virtual environments backed by [virtualenv](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv) or [UV](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv).
6|
7|## Configuration
8|
9|The environment plugin name is `virtual`.
10|
11|```toml config-example
12|[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]
13|type = "virtual"
14|```
15|
16|## Options
17|
18|| Option | Default | Description |
19|| --- | --- | --- |
20|| `python` | | The version of Python to find on your system and subsequently use to create the environment, defaulting to the `HATCH_PYTHON` environment variable, followed by the [normal resolution logic](#python-resolution). Setting the `HATCH_PYTHON` environment variable to `self` will force the use of the Python executable Hatch is running on. For more information, see the [documentation](https://virtualenv.pypa.io/en/latest/user_guide.html#python-discovery). |
21|| `python-sources` | `['external', 'internal']` | This may be set to an array of strings that are either the literal `internal` or `external`. External considers only Python executables that are already on `PATH`. Internal considers only [internally managed Python distributions](#internal-distributions). |
22|| `path` | | An explicit path to the virtual environment. The path may be absolute or relative to the project root. Any environments that [inherit](../../config/environment/overview.md#inheritance) this option will also use this path. The environment variable `HATCH_ENV_TYPE_VIRTUAL_PATH` may be used, which will take precedence. |
23|| `system-packages` | `false` | Whether or not to give the virtual environment access to the system `site-packages` directory |
24|| `installer` | `pip` | When set to `uv`, [UV](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) will be used in place of virtualenv & pip for virtual environment creation and dependency management, respectively. If you intend to provide UV yourself, you may set the `HATCH_ENV_TYPE_VIRTUAL_UV_PATH` environment variable which should be the absolute path to a UV binary. This environment variable implicitly sets the `installer` option to `uv` (if unset). |
25|
26|## Location
27|
28|The [location](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-find) of environments is determined in the following heuristic order:
29|
30|1. The `path` option
31|2. A directory named after the environment within the configured `virtual` [environment directory](../../config/hatch.md#environments) if the directory resides somewhere within the project root or if it is set to a `.virtualenvs` directory within the user's home directory
32|3. Otherwise, environments are stored within the configured `virtual` [environment directory](../../config/hatch.md#environments) in a deeply nested structure in order to support multiple projects
33|
34|Additionally, when the `path` option is not used, the name of the directory for the `default` environment will be the normalized project name to provide a more meaningful default [shell](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-shell) prompt.
35|
36|## Python resolution
37|
38|Virtual environments necessarily require a parent installation of Python. The following rules determine how the parent is resolved.
39|
40|The Python choice is determined by the [`python` option](#options) followed by the `HATCH_PYTHON` environment variable. If the choice is via the environment variable, then resolution stops and that path is used unconditionally.
41|
42|The resolvers will be based on the [`python-sources` option](#options) and all resolved interpreters will ensure compatibility with the project's defined [Python support](../../config/metadata.md#python-support).
43|
44|If a Python version has been chosen then each resolver will try to find an interpreter that satisfies that version.
45|
46|If no version has been chosen, then each resolver will try to find a version that matches the version of Python that Hatch is currently running on. If not found then each resolver will try to find the highest compatible version.
47|
48|!!! note
49|    Some external Python paths are considered unstable and are ignored during resolution. For example, if Hatch is installed via Homebrew then `sys.executable` will be ignored because the interpreter could change or be removed at any time.
50|
51|!!! note
52|    When resolution finds a match using an [internally managed distribution](#internal-distributions) and an update is available, the latest distribution will automatically be downloaded before environment creation.
53|
54|## Internal distributions
55|
56|The following options are recognized for internal Python resolution.
57|
58|!!! tip
59|    You can set custom sources for distributions by setting the `HATCH_PYTHON_SOURCE_<NAME>` environment variable where `<NAME>` is the uppercased version of the distribution name with periods replaced by underscores e.g. `HATCH_PYTHON_SOURCE_PYPY3_10`.

95|## Troubleshooting
96|
97|### macOS SIP
98|
99|If you need to set linker environment variables like those starting with `DYLD_` or `LD_`, any executable secured by [System Integrity Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_Integrity_Protection) that is invoked when [running commands](../../environment.md#command-execution) will not see those environment variable modifications as macOS strips those.
100|
101|Hatch interprets such commands as shell commands but deliberately ignores such paths to protected shells. This workaround suffices for the majority of use cases but there are 2 situations in which it may not:
102|
103|1. There are no unprotected `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, nor `fish` executables found along PATH.
104|2. The desired executable is a project's [script](../../config/metadata.md#cli), and the [location](#location) of environments contains spaces or is longer than 124[^1] characters. In this case `pip` and other installers will create such an entry point with a shebang pointing to `/bin/sh` (which is protected) to avoid shebang limitations. Rather than changing the location, you could invoke the script as e.g. `python -m pytest` (if the project supports that method of invocation by shipping a `__main__.py`).
105|
106|[^1]: The shebang length limit is [usually](https://web.archive.org/web/20221231220856/https://www.in-ulm.de/~mascheck/various/shebang/#length) 127 but 3 characters surround the executable path: `#!<EXE_PATH>\n`
