10|# Hatch v1.10.0
11|
12|Hatch [v1.10.0](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/releases/tag/hatch-v1.10.0) brings a test command, support for UV, and a Python script runner.
13|
14|<!-- more -->
15|
16|## Test command
17|
18|The new [`test`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-test) command allows you to easily run tests for your project on multiple versions of Python. The default behavior follows best practices, using [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) with select plugins for test execution and [coverage.py](https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy) for code coverage measurement.
19|
20|The command is designed to be both simple to use while also satisfying the needs of most projects. For example, the following shows Hatch running tests for [Jinja](https://github.com/pallets/jinja) in all environments in the [default matrix](../../config/internal/testing.md#matrix):
21|
22|<figure markdown>
23|  ![Testing Jinja example](release-hatch-1100/testing-jinja.gif){ loading=lazy role="img" }
24|</figure>
25|
26|Here is us testing [Rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich), with a bit of configuration:
27|
28|<figure markdown>
29|  ![Testing Rich example](release-hatch-1100/testing-rich.gif){ loading=lazy role="img" }
30|</figure>
31|
32|See the [tutorial](../../tutorials/testing/overview.md) for a detailed walk-through and the [config reference](../../config/internal/testing.md) for options.
33|
34|## UV
35|
36|The package installer [UV](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv), brought to you by the same folks behind [Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff), is now supported. In any environment, you can set the `installer` option to `uv` to use UV in place of [virtualenv](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv) & [pip](https://github.com/pypa/pip) for virtual environment creation and dependency management, respectively. This often results in a significant performance benefit.
37|
38|For example, if you wanted to enable this functionality for the [default](../../config/environment/overview.md#inheritance) environment, you could set the following:
39|
40|```toml config-example
41|[tool.hatch.envs.default]
42|installer = "uv"
43|```
44|
45|Semi-internal environments like those used for [testing](../../config/internal/testing.md) and [static analysis](../../config/internal/static-analysis.md) have this enabled by default.
46|
47|See the [how-to guide](../../how-to/environment/select-installer.md) for more information about switching the installer.
48|
49|## Python script runner
50|
51|The [`run`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-run) command now supports executing Python scripts with [inline metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/inline-script-metadata/) as standardized by [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/).
52|
53|As an example, consider the following script:
54|
55|```python tab="script.py"
56|# /// script
57|# requires-python = ">=3.11"
58|# dependencies = [
59|#   "httpx",
60|#   "rich",
61|# ]
62|# ///
63|
64|import httpx
65|from rich.pretty import pprint
66|
67|resp = httpx.get("https://peps.python.org/api/peps.json")
68|data = resp.json()
69|pprint([(k, v["title"]) for k, v in data.items()][:10])
70|```
71|
72|If you run the script for the first time as follows:
73|
74|```
75|hatch run script.py
76|```
77|
78|Hatch will create a dedicated environment for that script using a version of Python greater than or equal to 3.11 with dependencies `httpx` and `rich`.
79|
80|<figure markdown>
81|  ![Script running example](release-hatch-1100/run-script.gif){ loading=lazy role="img" }
82|</figure>
83|
84|See the [how-to guide](../../how-to/run/python-scripts.md) for more information.
85|
86|## Static analysis
87|
88|The environment used for static analysis is now [completely configurable](../../config/internal/static-analysis.md#customize-behavior) such that you can fully alter the underlying behavior of the [`fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-fmt) command (see the [how-to](../../how-to/static-analysis/behavior.md)).
89|
90|Additionally, Ruff has been updated to version 1.4.0 and the rules selected by default have been updated accordingly. Check out their [blog post](https://astral.sh/blog/ruff-v0.4.0) about how the new hand-written parser has made it twice as fast!
91|
92|## Community highlights
93|
94|### Visual Studio Code
95|
96|Visual Studio Code [announced support](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_88#_hatch-environment-discovery) for Hatch environments in their latest release. This means that you can now easily discover and select Hatch environments for your projects directly from the editor.
97|
98|See the [how-to guide](../../how-to/integrate/vscode.md) for detailed instructions.
99|
100|### CMake build plugin
101|
102|A [new release](https://github.com/scikit-build/scikit-build-core/releases/tag/v0.9.0) of the extension module builder [scikit-build-core](https://github.com/scikit-build/scikit-build-core) has introduced a [build plugin](https://scikit-build-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/plugins/hatchling.html) for Hatchling. This means that you can use Hatchling as your build backend while also shipping extension modules built with CMake.
103|
104|To get started, add the dependency to your [build requirements](../../config/build.md#build-system):
105|
106|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
107|[build-system]
108|requires = ["hatchling>=1.24.2", "scikit-build-core~=0.9.3"]
109|build-backend = "hatchling.build"
110|```
111|
112|Then explicitly enable the `experimental` option (acknowledging that the plugin will move to a dedicated package in the future):
113|
114|```toml config-example
115|[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.scikit-build]
116|experimental = true
117|```
118|
119|At this point, you can create your `CMakeLists.txt` file as usual and start building your extension modules with CMake! Check out the dedicated [example project](https://github.com/scikit-build/scikit-build-sample-projects/tree/main/projects/hatchling-pybind11-hello) for a complete demonstration.
120|
121|## Meta
122|
123|### Docs
124|
125|The efforts toward documentation improvements have increased substantially and the priorities have [shifted](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/issues/1245). From now on expect to see far more tutorials and how-to guides rather than just reference material.
126|
127|### Future
128|
129|Upcoming features include:
130|
131|- workspaces functionality [similar to Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch14-03-cargo-workspaces.html)
132|- commands to manage dependencies
133|- Windows release artifacts signed by the PSF (just like macOS)
134|- performance improvements for both the CLI and the Hatchling build system
135|
136|### Support
137|
138|If you or your organization finds value in what Hatch provides, consider a [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/ofek) to assist with maintenance and more rapid development!

48|                        continue

51|

53|

55|        config["license_expression"] = " OR ".join(license_data)
56|        config["license_header"] = (

58|            if not config["licenses"]["headers"]

60|# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: {self.creation_time.year}-present {config["name"]} <{config["email"]}>
61|#
62|# SPDX-License-Identifier: {config["license_expression"]}
63|"""
64|        )
65|        if len(license_ids) == 1:
66|            config["license_files"] = ""
67|        else:

69|

72|
73|        if not self.plugin_config["src-layout"]:

75|

77|        files = list(find_template_files(files_default))
78|
79|        # Add any licenses

81|        if license_data:
82|            if len(license_data) == 1:
83|                license_id, text = next(iter(license_data.items()))
84|                license_text = get_license_text(config, license_id, text, self.creation_time)
85|                files.append(File(Path("LICENSE.txt"), license_text))
86|            else:

88|                for license_id, text in license_data.items():
89|                    license_text = get_license_text(config, license_id, text, self.creation_time)
90|                    files.append(File(Path("LICENSES", f"{license_id}.txt"), license_text))
91|
92|        if config["args"]["cli"]:
93|            from hatch.template import files_feature_cli
94|
95|            files.extend(find_template_files(files_feature_cli))
96|
97|        if self.plugin_config["tests"]:
98|            from hatch.template import files_feature_tests
99|
100|            files.extend(find_template_files(files_feature_tests))
101|
102|        if self.plugin_config["ci"]:
103|            from hatch.template import files_feature_ci
104|
105|            files.extend(find_template_files(files_feature_ci))
106|
107|        return files
108|
109|    def finalize_files(self, config, files):
110|        if config["licenses"]["headers"] and config["license_data"]:
111|            for template_file in files:
112|                if template_file.path.name.endswith(".py"):
113|                    template_file.contents = config["license_header"] + template_file.contents
114|
115|        if self.plugin_config["src-layout"]:
116|            for template_file in files:
117|                if template_file.path.parts[0] == config["package_name"]:

119|
120|
121|def get_license_text(config, license_id, license_text, creation_time):
122|    if license_id == "MIT":
123|        license_text = license_text.replace("<year>", f"{creation_time.year}-present", 1)
124|        license_text = license_text.replace("<copyright holders>", f"{config['name']} <{config['email']}>", 1)

9|

12|

14|def filter_environments(environments, filter_data):
15|    selected_environments = []
16|    for env_name, env_data in environments.items():
17|        for key, value in filter_data.items():
18|            if key not in env_data or env_data[key] != value:
19|                break
20|        else:
21|            selected_environments.append(env_name)

26|@click.command(short_help="Run commands within project environments")
27|@click.argument("args", required=True, nargs=-1)
28|@click.option("--env", "-e", "env_names", multiple=True, help="The environments to target")
29|@click.option("--include", "-i", "included_variable_specs", multiple=True, help="The matrix variables to include")
30|@click.option("--exclude", "-x", "excluded_variable_specs", multiple=True, help="The matrix variables to exclude")
31|@click.option("--filter", "-f", "filter_json", default=None, help="The JSON data used to select environments")
32|@click.option(
33|    "--force-continue", is_flag=True, help="Run every command and if there were any errors exit with the first code"
34|)
35|@click.option("--ignore-compat", is_flag=True, help="Ignore incompatibility when selecting specific environments")
36|@click.pass_obj
37|def run(
38|    app: Application,
39|    *,
40|    args: tuple[str, ...],
41|    env_names: tuple[str, ...],
42|    included_variable_specs: tuple[str, ...],
43|    excluded_variable_specs: tuple[str, ...],
44|    filter_json: str | None,
45|    force_continue: bool,
46|    ignore_compat: bool,
47|):
48|    """
49|    Run commands within project environments.
50|
51|    The `-e`/`--env` option overrides the equivalent [root option](#hatch) and the `HATCH_ENV` environment variable.
52|
53|    The `-i`/`--include` and `-x`/`--exclude` options may be used to include or exclude certain
54|    variables, optionally followed by specific comma-separated values, and may be selected multiple
55|    times. For example, if you have the following configuration:
56|
57|    \b
58|    ```toml config-example
59|    [[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
60|    python = ["3.9", "3.10"]
61|    version = ["42", "3.14", "9000"]
62|    ```
63|
64|    then running:
65|
66|    \b
67|    ```
68|    hatch env run -i py=3.10 -x version=9000 test:pytest
69|    ```
70|
71|    would execute `pytest` in the environments `test.py3.10-42` and `test.py3.10-3.14`.
72|    Note that `py` may be used as an alias for `python`.
73|
74|    \b
75|    !!! note
76|        The inclusion option is treated as an intersection while the exclusion option is treated as a
77|        union i.e. an environment must match all of the included variables to be selected while matching
78|        any of the excluded variables will prevent selection.
79|    """
80|    from hatch.utils.runner import parse_matrix_variables, select_environments
81|
82|    try:
83|        included_variables = parse_matrix_variables(included_variable_specs)
84|    except ValueError as e:
85|        app.abort(f"Duplicate included variable: {e}")
86|
87|    try:
88|        excluded_variables = parse_matrix_variables(excluded_variable_specs)
89|    except ValueError as e:
90|        app.abort(f"Duplicate excluded variable: {e}")
91|
92|    app.ensure_environment_plugin_dependencies()
93|
94|    project = app.project
95|
96|    if not env_names:
97|        env_names = (app.env,)
98|    elif "system" in env_names:
99|        project.config.config["envs"] = {
100|            "system": {
101|                "type": "system",
102|                "skip-install": True,
103|                "scripts": project.config.scripts,
104|            }
105|        }
106|
107|    # Deduplicate
108|    ordered_env_names = list(dict.fromkeys(env_names))
109|
110|    environments = []
111|    matrix_selected = False
112|    for env_name in ordered_env_names:
113|        if env_name in project.config.matrices:
114|            matrix_selected = True
115|            env_data = project.config.matrices[env_name]["envs"]
116|            if not env_data:
117|                app.abort(f"No variables defined for matrix: {env_name}")
118|
119|            environments.extend(select_environments(env_data, included_variables, excluded_variables))
120|        else:
121|            environments.append(env_name)
122|
123|    if filter_json:
124|        import json
125|
126|        filter_data = json.loads(filter_json)
127|        if not isinstance(filter_data, dict):
128|            app.abort("The --filter/-f option must be a JSON mapping")
129|
130|        environments[:] = filter_environments(project.config.envs, filter_data)
131|
132|    if not environments:
133|        app.abort("No environments were selected")
134|    elif not matrix_selected and (included_variables or excluded_variables):
135|        app.abort(f"Variable selection is unsupported for non-matrix environments: {', '.join(ordered_env_names)}")
136|
137|    for context in app.runner_context(
138|        environments,
139|        ignore_compat=ignore_compat or matrix_selected,
140|        display_header=matrix_selected,
141|        keep_env=bool(os.environ.get(AppEnvVars.KEEP_ENV)),
142|    ):
143|        if context.env.name == "system":
144|            context.env.exists = lambda: True  # type: ignore[method-assign]
145|
146|        context.force_continue = force_continue
147|        context.add_shell_command(list(args))

1|# Environment sources
2|
3|-----
4|
5|The `sources` table of an environment redirects dependencies to alternative origins at install time without changing your project's published metadata. This is useful during development when you want to consume a dependency from a local checkout, a Git branch, a private index, or another workspace member, while keeping the released wheel pointing at the version you ship.
6|
7|A source is matched against your dependencies by name, after [PEP 503 normalization](https://peps.python.org/pep-0503/#normalized-names). Both [project dependencies](../metadata.md#dependencies) and [environment dependencies](overview.md#dependencies) are eligible for redirection.
8|
9|```toml config-example
10|[project]
11|dependencies = ["foo"]
12|
13|[tool.hatch.envs.default.sources]
14|foo = "./packages/foo"
15|```
16|
17|The top-level `[tool.hatch.sources]` table is an alias for the `default` environment, so the following is equivalent:
18|
19|```toml config-example
20|[tool.hatch.sources]
21|foo = "./packages/foo"
22|```
23|
24|!!! note
25|    Sources only affect installs performed by Hatch when it manages an environment. They do not influence the metadata of wheels you build with `hatch build`.
26|
27|## Inheritance
28|
29|Sources follow the usual [inheritance](overview.md#inheritance) rules, merging entry by entry so that an environment can redirect a single dependency differently while every other entry it inherits stays in place:
30|
31|```toml config-example
32|[tool.hatch.sources]
33|foo = "./packages/foo"
34|bar = "./packages/bar"
35|
36|[tool.hatch.envs.test-upstream.sources]
37|foo = { git = "https://github.com/example/foo", branch = "main" }
38|```
39|
40|Here every environment installs both `foo` and `bar` from the local checkouts, except `test-upstream`, which keeps the local `bar` but tracks the upstream development branch of `foo`.
41|
42|An environment that does not inherit from `default`, such as a [detached](overview.md#detached-environments) one, receives no sources.
43|
44|## Path
45|
46|Use a relative or absolute path to a wheel, source distribution, or project directory:
47|
48|```toml config-example
49|[tool.hatch.sources]
50|foo = "./packages/foo"
51|```
52|
53|The shorthand above is equivalent to the full form:
54|
55|```toml config-example
56|[tool.hatch.sources]
57|foo = { path = "./packages/foo", editable = true }
58|```
59|
60|`editable` defaults to `true` to match Hatch's existing handling of local installs. Set `editable = false` for a non-editable install. If the package lives below the path root, set `subdirectory`:
61|
62|```toml config-example
63|[tool.hatch.sources]
64|foo = { path = "./monorepo", subdirectory = "packages/foo" }
65|```
66|
67|For editable installs the subdirectory is resolved into the path itself (equivalent to `path = "./monorepo/packages/foo"`), since installers expect a bare project directory. For non-editable installs the subdirectory is passed as a URL fragment, which also supports archives.
68|
69|## Git
70|
71|Pull from a Git repository:
72|
73|```toml config-example
74|[tool.hatch.sources]
75|foo = { git = "https://github.com/example/foo" }
76|```
77|
78|Pin to a specific revision with one of `rev`, `tag`, or `branch` (mutually exclusive):
79|
80|```toml config-example
81|[tool.hatch.sources]
82|foo = { git = "https://github.com/example/foo", rev = "abc1234" }
83|bar = { git = "https://github.com/example/bar", tag = "v1.0" }
84|baz = { git = "https://github.com/example/baz", branch = "main" }
85|```
86|
87|Use `subdirectory` when the Python package is not at the repository root.
88|
89|## URL
90|
91|Install a wheel or source archive from a URL:
92|
93|```toml config-example
94|[tool.hatch.sources]
95|foo = { url = "https://files.example.com/foo-1.0.tar.gz" }
96|```
97|
98|`subdirectory` is also supported for archives where the package is not at the root.
99|
100|## Index
101|
102|Resolve the dependency from a specific package index:
103|
104|```toml config-example
105|[tool.hatch.sources]
106|foo = { index = "https://pypi.example.com/simple" }
107|```
108|
109|The index URL is passed to the installer as `--extra-index-url`, so the default index (PyPI) remains the primary source. Multiple index sources are deduplicated and order-preserving.
110|
111|## Workspace
112|
113|Resolve the dependency from a [workspace](../../how-to/environment/workspace.md) member:
114|
115|```toml config-example
116|[tool.hatch.sources]
117|my-pkg = { workspace = true }
118|```
119|
120|The actual install path is determined by the matching member in `tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>.workspace.members`. This lets you declare workspace membership in one place and reference it from many environments.
121|
122|## Precedence
123|
124|A dependency that already uses a [PEP 508 direct reference](../dependency.md#direct-references) is left untouched — the explicit URL on the dependency wins over a configured source.
125|
126|## Disabling sources
127|
128|Setting the `HATCH_NO_SOURCES` environment variable to any non-empty value disables all sources. This is useful in CI to verify that your published metadata resolves on its own, without local redirections:
129|
130|```
131|HATCH_NO_SOURCES=1 hatch env create
132|```
133|
134|## Inspecting sources
135|
136|The [`dep show sources`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-show) command displays each configured source, its target, and the dependencies of the active environment that it redirects. Sources that match no dependencies are reported with a warning, which helps catch typos in source names since unmatched sources are otherwise silently ignored.
137|
138|## Installer translation
139|
140|Sources produce installer-agnostic instructions that Hatch renders into the right flags for the configured installer:
141|
142|| Source | Per-dependency form | Global flags |
143|| --- | --- | --- |
144|| `path` (editable) | `--editable <resolved>` | none |
145|| `path` (non-editable) | `name @ file://<resolved>` | none |
146|| `git` | `name @ git+<url>[@<ref>]` | none |
147|| `url` | `name @ <url>` | none |
148|| `index` | unchanged | `--extra-index-url <url>` |
149|| `workspace` | resolved through `workspace.members` | none |
150|
151|Both [`installer = "pip"`](overview.md#dependencies) and `installer = "uv"` accept the same flag forms, so the same source configuration works for either. When an environment is [`locked`](overview.md#locked), sources also apply during lock resolution: rewritten requirements flow into the lock inputs and index sources are passed to the resolver as `--extra-index-url`.
152|
153|!!! note
154|    Sources do not apply to [build requirements](../build.md#build-system) (`build-system.requires` or build target dependencies). Build environments always resolve from declared metadata so that builds remain reproducible.

1|# Environments
2|
3|-----
4|
5|[Environments](config/environment/overview.md) are designed to allow for isolated workspaces for testing, building documentation, or anything else projects need.
6|
7|Unless an environment is [chosen explicitly](#selection), Hatch will use the `default` environment.
8|
9|!!! tip
10|    For a more comprehensive walk-through, see the [Basic usage](tutorials/environment/basic-usage.md) tutorial.
11|
12|## Creation
13|
14|You can create environments by using the [`env create`](cli/reference.md#hatch-env-create) command. Let's enter the directory of the project we created in the [setup phase](intro.md#new-project):
15|
16|```console
17|$ hatch env create
18|Creating environment: default
19|Installing project in development mode
20|Syncing dependencies
21|```
22|
23|!!! tip
24|    You never need to manually create environments as [spawning a shell](#entering-environments) or [running commands](#command-execution) within one will automatically trigger creation.
25|
26|## Entering environments
27|
28|You can spawn a [shell](config/hatch.md#shell) within an environment by using the [`shell`](cli/reference.md#hatch-shell) command.
29|
30|```console
31|$ hatch shell
32|(hatch-demo) $
33|```
34|
35|Now confirm the project has been installed:
36|
37|```console
38|(hatch-demo) $ pip show hatch-demo
39|Name: hatch-demo
40|Version: 0.0.1
41|...
42|```
43|
44|Finally, see where your environment's Python is [located](config/hatch.md#environments):
45|
46|```console
47|(hatch-demo) $ python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"
48|...
49|```
50|
51|You can type `exit` to leave the environment.
52|
53|## Command execution
54|
55|The [`run`](cli/reference.md#hatch-run) command allows you to execute commands in an environment as if you had already entered it. For example, running the following command will output the same path as before:
56|
57|```
58|hatch run python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"
59|```
60|
61|!!! tip
62|    Be sure to check out how to define [scripts](config/environment/overview.md#scripts) for your project.
63|
64|## Dependencies
65|
66|Hatch ensures that environments are always compatible with the currently defined [project dependencies](config/metadata.md#dependencies) (if [installed](config/environment/overview.md#skip-install) and in [dev mode](config/environment/overview.md#dev-mode)) and [environment dependencies](config/environment/overview.md#dependencies).
67|
68|To add `cowsay` as a dependency, open `pyproject.toml` and add it to the [`dependencies`](config/metadata.md#dependencies) array:
69|
70|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
71|[project]
72|...
73|dependencies = [
74|  "cowsay"
75|]
76|```
77|
78|This dependency will be installed the next time you [spawn a shell](#entering-environments) or [run a command](#command-execution). For example:
79|
80|```console
81|$ hatch run cowsay -t "Hello, world!"
82|Syncing dependencies
83|  _____________
84|| Hello, world! |
85|  =============
86|             \
87|              \
88|                ^__^
89|                (oo)\_______
90|                (__)\       )\/\
91|                    ||----w |
92|                    ||     ||
93|```
94|
95|!!! note
96|    The `Syncing dependencies` status will display temporarily when Hatch updates environments in response to any dependency changes that you make.
97|
98|## Locking
99|
100|Hatch can generate [PEP 751](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/) lockfiles (`pylock.toml`) for environments. Configure environments with [`locked = true`](config/environment/overview.md#locked) and then use the [`env lock`](cli/reference.md#hatch-env-lock) command, or [`dep lock`](cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-lock) / [`lock`](cli/reference.md#hatch-lock) for the active environment:
101|
102|```console
103|$ hatch env lock
104|Locking environment: default
105|Wrote lockfile: /path/to/project/pylock.toml
106|```
107|
108|When called without arguments, all environments configured with `locked = true` will be locked. Environments are also locked automatically when created or when their dependencies change. See the [lockfile how-to guide](how-to/environment/lockfiles.md) for more details.
109|
110|## Selection
111|
112|You can select which environment to enter or run commands in by using the `-e`/`--env` [root option](cli/reference.md#hatch) or by setting the `HATCH_ENV` environment variable.
113|
114|The [`run`](cli/reference.md#hatch-run) command allows for more explicit selection by prepending `<ENV_NAME>:` to commands. For example, if you had the following configuration:
115|
116|```toml config-example
117|[tool.hatch.envs.docs]
118|dependencies = [
119|  "mkdocs"
120|]
121|[tool.hatch.envs.docs.scripts]
122|build = "mkdocs build --clean --strict"
123|serve = "mkdocs serve --dev-addr localhost:8000"
124|```
125|
126|you could then serve your documentation by running:
127|
128|```
129|hatch run docs:serve
130|```
131|
132|!!! tip
133|    If you've already [entered](#entering-environments) an environment, commands will target it by default.
134|
135|## Matrix
136|
137|Every environment can define its own set of [matrices](config/environment/advanced.md#matrix):
138|
139|```toml config-example
140|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
141|dependencies = [
142|  "pytest"
143|]
144|
145|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
146|python = ["3.10", "3.11"]
147|version = ["42", "3.14"]
148|
149|[[tool.hatch.envs.test.matrix]]
150|python = ["3.11", "3.12"]
151|version = ["9000"]
152|feature = ["foo", "bar"]
153|```
154|
155|Using the [`env show`](cli/reference.md#hatch-env-show) command would then display:
156|
157|```console
158|$ hatch env show --ascii
159|     Standalone
160|+---------+---------+
161|| Name    | Type    |
162|+=========+=========+
163|| default | virtual |
164|+---------+---------+
165|                        Matrices
166|+------+---------+----------------------+--------------+
167|| Name | Type    | Envs                 | Dependencies |
168|+======+=========+======================+==============+
169|| test | virtual | test.py3.10-42       | pytest       |
170||      |         | test.py3.10-3.14     |              |
171||      |         | test.py3.11-42       |              |
172||      |         | test.py3.11-3.14     |              |
173||      |         | test.py3.11-9000-foo |              |
174||      |         | test.py3.11-9000-bar |              |
175||      |         | test.py3.12-9000-foo |              |
176||      |         | test.py3.12-9000-bar |              |
177|+------+---------+----------------------+--------------+
178|```
179|
180|## Removal
181|
182|You can remove a single environment or environment matrix by using the [`env remove`](cli/reference.md#hatch-env-remove) command or all of a project's environments by using the [`env prune`](cli/reference.md#hatch-env-prune) command.

11|def ensure_path_public(path: str, shells: list[str]) -> bool:
12|    import userpath
13|
14|    if userpath.in_current_path(path) or userpath.in_new_path(path, shells):
15|        return True
16|

21|@click.command(short_help="Install Python distributions")
22|@click.argument("names", required=True, nargs=-1)
23|@click.option("--private", is_flag=True, help="Do not add distributions to the user PATH")
24|@click.option("--update", "-u", is_flag=True, help="Update existing installations")
25|@click.option(
26|    "--dir", "-d", "directory", help="The directory in which to install distributions, overriding configuration"
27|)
28|@click.pass_obj
29|def install(app: Application, *, names: tuple[str, ...], private: bool, update: bool, directory: str | None):
30|    """
31|    Install Python distributions.
32|
33|    You may select `all` to install all compatible distributions:
34|
35|    \b
36|    ```
37|    hatch python install all
38|    ```
39|
40|    You can set custom sources for distributions by setting the `HATCH_PYTHON_SOURCE_<NAME>` environment variable
41|    where `<NAME>` is the uppercased version of the distribution name with periods replaced by underscores e.g.
42|    `HATCH_PYTHON_SOURCE_PYPY3_10`.
43|    """
44|    from hatch.errors import PythonDistributionResolutionError, PythonDistributionUnknownError
45|    from hatch.python.distributions import ORDERED_DISTRIBUTIONS
46|    from hatch.python.resolve import get_distribution
47|
48|    shells = []
49|    if not private and not app.platform.windows:
50|        shell_name, _ = app.shell_data
51|        shells.append(shell_name)
52|
53|    manager = app.get_python_manager(directory)
54|    installed = manager.get_installed()
55|    selection = ORDERED_DISTRIBUTIONS if "all" in names else names
56|    unknown = []
57|    compatible = []
58|    incompatible = []
59|    for name in selection:
60|        if name in installed:
61|            compatible.append(name)
62|            continue
63|
64|        try:
65|            get_distribution(name)
66|        except PythonDistributionUnknownError:
67|            unknown.append(name)
68|        except PythonDistributionResolutionError:
69|            incompatible.append(name)
70|        else:
71|            compatible.append(name)
72|
73|    if unknown:
74|        app.abort(f"Unknown distributions: {', '.join(unknown)}")
75|    elif incompatible and (not compatible or "all" not in names):
76|        app.abort(f"Incompatible distributions: {', '.join(incompatible)}")
77|
78|    directories_made_public = []
79|    for name in compatible:
80|        needs_update = False
81|        if name in installed:
82|            installed_dist = installed[name]
83|            needs_update = installed_dist.needs_update()
84|            if not needs_update:
85|                app.display_warning(f"The latest version is already installed: {installed_dist.version}")
86|                continue
87|
88|            if not (update or app.confirm(f"Update {name}?")):
89|                app.abort(f"Distribution is already installed: {name}")
90|
91|        with app.status(f"{'Updating' if needs_update else 'Installing'} {name}"):
92|            dist = manager.install(name)
93|            if not private:
94|                python_directory = str(dist.python_path.parent)
95|                if not ensure_path_public(python_directory, shells=shells):
96|                    directories_made_public.append(python_directory)
97|
98|        app.display_success(f"{'Updated' if needs_update else 'Installed'} {name} @ {dist.path}")
99|
100|    if directories_made_public:
101|        multiple = len(directories_made_public) > 1
102|        app.display(
103|            f"\nThe following director{'ies' if multiple else 'y'} ha{'ve' if multiple else 's'} "
104|            f"been added to your PATH (pending a shell restart):\n"
105|        )
106|        for public_directory in directories_made_public:
107|            app.display(public_directory)

1|# Managing environments
2|
3|-----
4|
5|Hatch [environments](../../environment.md) are isolated workspaces that can be used for project tasks including running tests, building documentation and running code formatters and linters.
6|
7|## The default environment
8|
9|When you start using Hatch, you can create the `default` environment. To do this use the [`env create`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-create) command:
10|
11|```
12|hatch env create
13|```
14|
15|This will not only create will the `default` environment for you to work in but will also install your project in [dev mode](../../config/environment/overview.md#dev-mode) in this `default` environment.
16|
17|!!! tip
18|    You never need to manually create environments as [spawning a shell](#launching-a-shell-within-a-specific-environment) or [running commands](#run-commands-within-a-specific-environment) within one will automatically trigger creation.
19|
20|### Using the default environment
21|
22|Hatch will always use the `default` environment if an environment is not chosen explicitly when [running a command](../../environment.md#command-execution).
23|
24|For instance, the following shows how to get version information for the Python in use.
25|
26|```console
27|$ hatch run python -V
28|Python 3.12.1
29|```
30|
31|### Configure the default environment
32|
33|You can customize the tools that are installed into the `default` environment by adding a table called `tool.hatch.envs.default` to your `pyproject.toml` file. Below is an example of adding the [dependencies](../../config/environment/overview.md#dependencies) `pydantic` and `numpy` to the `default` environment.
34|
35|```toml config-example
36|[tool.hatch.envs.default]
37|dependencies = [
38|  "pydantic",
39|  "numpy",
40|]
41|```
42|
43|You can declare versions for your dependencies as well within this configuration.
44|
45|```toml config-example
46|[tool.hatch.envs.default]
47|dependencies = [
48|  "pydantic>=2.0",
49|  "numpy",
50|]
51|```
52|
53|## Create custom environment
54|
55|You can create custom environments in Hatch by adding a section to your `pyproject.toml` file `[tool.hatch.envs.<ENV_NAME>]`. Below you define an environment called `test` and you add the `pytest` and `pytest-cov` dependencies to that environment's configuration.
56|
57|```toml config-example
58|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
59|dependencies = [
60|  "pytest",
61|  "pytest-cov"
62|]
63|```
64|
65|The first time that you call the test environment, Hatch will:
66|
67|1. Create the environment
68|2. Install your project into that environment in [dev mode](../../config/environment/overview.md#dev-mode) (by default) along with its [dependencies](../../config/metadata.md#dependencies).
69|3. Install the environment's [dependencies](../../config/environment/overview.md#dependencies)
70|
71|## Run commands within a specific environment
72|
73|Hatch offers a unique environment feature that allows you run a specific command within a specific environment rather than needing to activate the environment as you would using a tool such as [Conda](https://conda.org) or [venv](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html).
74|
75|For instance, if you define an environment called `test` that contains the dependencies from the previous section, you can run the `pytest` command from the `test` environment using the syntax:
76|
77|```
78|hatch run <ENV_NAME>:command
79|```
80|
81|To access the `test` environment and run `pytest`, you can run:
82|
83|```console
84|$ hatch run test:pytest
85|============================== test session starts ===============================
86|platform darwin -- Python 3.12.1, pytest-7.4.4, pluggy-1.3.0
87|rootdir: /your/path/to/yourproject
88|collected 0 items
89|```
90|
91|!!! note
92|    `test:pytest` represents the name of the environment to call (`test`) and the command to run (`pytest`).
93|
94|## View current environments
95|
96|Above you defined and created a new test environment in your `pyproject.toml` file. You can now use the [`env show`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-show) command to see both the currently created environments and the dependencies in each environment.
97|
98|```
99|$ hatch env show
100|             Standalone
101|┏━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
102|┃ Name    ┃ Type    ┃ Dependencies ┃
103|┡━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
104|│ default │ virtual │              │
105|├─────────┼─────────┼──────────────┤
106|│ test    │ virtual │ pytest       │
107|│         │         │ pytest-cov   │
108|└─────────┴─────────┴──────────────┘
109|```
110|
111|!!! note
112|    The output may have more columns depending on your environment configuration.
113|
114|## Locating environments
115|
116|To see where your current environment is located you can use the [`env find`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-find) command.
117|
118|```
119|$ hatch env find test
120|/your/path/Application Support/hatch/env/virtual/yourproject/twO2iQR3/test
121|```
122|
123|!!! note
124|    That path is what you would see on macOS but differs for each platform, and is [configurable](../../plugins/environment/virtual.md#location).
125|
126|## Launching a shell within a specific environment
127|
128|If you wish to [launch a shell](../../environment.md#entering-environments) for a specific environment that you have created, like the previous `test` environment, you can use:
129|
130|```
131|hatch -e test shell
132|```
133|
134|Once the environment is active, you can run commands like you would in any Python environment.
135|
136|Notice below that when running `pip list` in the test environment, you can see:
137|
138|1. That your package is installed in editable mode.
139|2. That the environment contains both `pytest` and `pytest-cov` as specified above in the `pyproject.toml` file.
140|
141|```
142|$ pip list
143|Package     Version Editable project location
144|----------- ------- ----------------------------------------------------
145|coverage    7.4.1
146|iniconfig   2.0.0
147|packaging   23.2
148|pip         23.3.1
149|pluggy      1.4.0
150|pytest      8.0.0
151|pytest-cov  4.1.0
152|yourproject 0.1.0  /your/path/to/yourproject
153|```
154|
155|## Conda environments
156|
157|If you prefer to use [Conda](https://conda.org) environments with Hatch, you can check out the [hatch-conda plugin](https://github.com/OldGrumpyViking/hatch-conda).

11|def get_install_source(platform_name: str) -> str:
12|    import os
13|    import sys
14|    import sysconfig
15|
16|    from platformdirs import user_data_dir
17|
18|    from hatch.utils.fs import Path
19|
20|    default_source = "pip"
21|
22|    python_path = Path(sys.executable).resolve()
23|    parent_paths = python_path.parents
24|
25|    # https://github.com/ofek/pyapp/blob/v0.13.0/src/app.rs#L27
26|    if Path(user_data_dir("pyapp", appauthor=False)) in parent_paths:
27|        return "binary"
28|
29|    # https://pypa.github.io/pipx/how-pipx-works/
30|    if (Path.home() / ".local" / "pipx" / "venvs") in parent_paths:
31|        return "pipx"
32|
33|    # https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/externally-managed-environments/#marking-an-interpreter-as-using-an-external-package-manager
34|    try:
35|        stdlib_path_config = sysconfig.get_path("stdlib")
36|    # https://docs.python.org/3/library/sysconfig.html#sysconfig.get_path
37|    except KeyError:
38|        stdlib_path_config = ""
39|
40|    if (
41|        # This does not work on NixOS, see: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/201037
42|        sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix
43|        and stdlib_path_config
44|        and (stdlib_path := Path(stdlib_path_config)).is_dir()
45|        and any(p.name == "EXTERNALLY-MANAGED" and p.is_file() for p in stdlib_path.iterdir())
46|    ):
47|        return "system"
48|
49|    if platform_name == "windows":
50|        if sys.executable.endswith("WindowsApps\\python.exe"):
51|            return "Windows Store"
52|
53|        # Break early because nothing after is applicable
54|        return default_source
55|
56|    if platform_name == "macos" and Path("/usr/local/Cellar") in parent_paths:  # no cov
57|        return "Homebrew"
58|
59|    # https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv/tree/v2.3.35#set-up-your-shell-environment-for-pyenv
60|    if Path(os.environ.get("PYENV_ROOT", "~/.pyenv")).expand() in parent_paths:
61|        return "Pyenv"
62|
63|    return default_source

66|@click.command(short_help="Generate a pre-populated GitHub issue")
67|@click.option("--no-open", "-n", is_flag=True, help="Show the URL instead of opening it")
68|@click.pass_obj
69|def report(app: Application, *, no_open: bool) -> None:
70|    """Generate a pre-populated GitHub issue."""
71|    import sys
72|    import webbrowser
73|    from textwrap import indent
74|    from urllib.parse import quote_plus
75|
76|    import tomlkit
77|
78|    from hatch._version import __version__
79|    from hatch.utils.toml import load_toml_data
80|
81|    # Retain the config that would be most useful
82|    full_config = load_toml_data(app.config_file.read_scrubbed())
83|    relevant_config: dict[str, Any] = {}
84|    for setting in ("mode", "shell"):
85|        if setting in full_config:
86|            relevant_config[setting] = full_config[setting]
87|
88|    full_dirs = full_config.get("dirs")
89|    if isinstance(full_dirs, dict) and (env_dirs := full_dirs.get("envs")):
90|        relevant_config["dirs"] = {"envs": env_dirs}
91|
92|    # Try to determine how Hatch was installed
93|    source = get_install_source(app.platform.name)
94|
95|    element_padding = " " * 4
96|    body = f"""\
97|## Current behavior
98|<!-- A clear and concise description of the behavior. -->
99|
100|## Expected behavior
101|<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
102|
103|## Additional context
104|<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. If applicable, add screenshots to help explain. -->
105|
106|## Debug
107|
108|### Installation
109|
110|- Source: {source}
111|- Version: {__version__}
112|- Platform: {app.platform.display_name}
113|- Python version:
114|{element_padding}```
115|{indent(sys.version, element_padding)}
116|{element_padding}```
117|
118|### Configuration
119|
120|```toml
121|{tomlkit.dumps(relevant_config).rstrip()}
122|```
123|"""
124|
125|    url = f"https://github.com/pypa/hatch/issues/new?body={quote_plus(body)}"
126|    if no_open:
127|        app.display(url)
128|    else:
129|        webbrowser.open_new_tab(url)

1|from __future__ import annotations
2|
3|from hatch.utils.fs import Path
4|
5|
6|class AuthenticationCredentials:
7|    def __init__(
8|        self,
9|        app,
10|        cache_dir: Path,
11|        options: dict,
12|        repo: str,
13|        repo_config: dict[str, str],
14|    ):
15|        self._app = app
16|        self._pwu_path = cache_dir / "previous_working_users.json"
17|        self._options = options
18|        self._repo = repo
19|        self._repo_config = repo_config
20|
21|        self.__username: str | None = None
22|        self.__password: str | None = None
23|        self.__username_was_read = False
24|        self.__password_was_read = False
25|        self.__pwu_data: dict[str, str] = {}
26|
27|    @property
28|    def password(self) -> str:
29|        if self.__password is None:
30|            self.__password = self.__get_password()
31|        return self.__password
32|
33|    @property
34|    def username(self) -> str:
35|        if self.__username is None:
36|            self.__username = self.__get_username()
37|        return self.__username
38|
39|    def __get_password(self) -> str:
40|        # this method doesn't consider .pypirc as the __password attribute would have
41|        # been set when it was looked up during username retrieval
42|
43|        password = self._options.get("auth") or self._repo_config.get("auth")
44|        if password is not None:
45|            return password
46|
47|        import keyring
48|
49|        keyring_service = self._repo_config["url"]
50|        password = keyring.get_password(keyring_service, self.username)
51|        if password is not None:
52|            return password
53|
54|        if self._options["no_prompt"]:
55|            self._app.abort("Missing required option: auth")
56|
57|        self.__password_was_read = True
58|        return self._app.prompt("Password / Token", hide_input=True)
59|
60|    def __get_username(self) -> str:
61|        username = (
62|            self._options.get("user")
63|            or self._repo_config.get("user")
64|            or self._read_pypirc()
65|            or self._read_previous_working_user_data()
66|        )
67|        if username is not None:
68|            return username
69|
70|        if self._options["no_prompt"]:
71|            self._app.abort("Missing required option: user")
72|
73|        self.__username_was_read = True
74|        return self._app.prompt(f"Username for '{self._repo_config['url']}' [__token__]") or "__token__"
75|
76|    def _read_previous_working_user_data(self) -> str | None:
77|        if self._pwu_path.is_file():
78|            contents = self._pwu_path.read_text()
79|            if contents:
80|                import json
81|
82|                self.__pwu_data = json.loads(contents)
83|        return self.__pwu_data.get(self._repo)
84|
85|    def _read_pypirc(self) -> str | None:
86|        import configparser
87|
88|        pypirc = configparser.ConfigParser()
89|        pypirc.read(Path.home() / ".pypirc")
90|        repo = self._repo or "pypi"
91|
92|        if pypirc.has_section(repo):
93|            self.__password = pypirc.get(section=repo, option="password", fallback=None)
94|            return pypirc.get(section=repo, option="username", fallback=None)
95|
96|        repo_url = self._repo_config["url"]
97|        for section in pypirc.sections():
98|            if pypirc.get(section=section, option="repository", fallback=None) == repo_url:
99|                self.__password = pypirc.get(section=section, option="password", fallback=None)
100|                return pypirc.get(section=section, option="username", fallback=None)
101|
102|        return None
103|
104|    def write_updated_data(self):
105|        if self.__username_was_read:
106|            import json
107|
108|            self.__pwu_data[self._repo] = self.__username
109|            self._pwu_path.ensure_parent_dir_exists()
110|            self._pwu_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.__pwu_data))
111|
112|        if self.__password_was_read:
113|            import keyring
114|
115|            keyring_service = self._repo_config["url"]
116|            keyring.set_password(keyring_service, self.__username, self.__password)

1|# Configuring project metadata
2|
3|-----
4|
5|Project metadata is stored in a `pyproject.toml` file located at the root of a project's tree
6|and is based entirely on [the standard][project metadata standard].
7|
8|## Name (*required*) ## {: #name }
9|
10|The name of the project.
11|
12|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
13|[project]
14|name = "your-app"
15|```
16|
17|## Version (*required*) ## {: #version }
18|
19|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: pyproject.toml"
20|
21|    === "Dynamic"
22|        See the dedicated [versioning](../version.md) section.
23|
24|        ```toml
25|        [project]
26|        ...
27|        dynamic = ["version"]
28|
29|        [tool.hatch.version]
30|        path = "..."
31|        ```
32|
33|    === "Static"
34|        ```toml
35|        [project]
36|        ...
37|        version = "0.0.1"
38|        ```
39|
40|## Description
41|
42|A brief summary of the project.
43|
44|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
45|[project]
46|...
47|description = '...'
48|```
49|
50|## Readme
51|
52|The full description of the project.
53|
54|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: pyproject.toml"
55|
56|    === "Simple"
57|        The file extension must be `.md`, `.rst`, or `.txt`.
58|
59|        ```toml
60|        [project]
61|        ...
62|        readme = "README.md"
63|        ```
64|
65|    === "Complex"
66|        The `content-type` field must be set to `text/markdown`, `text/x-rst`, or `text/plain`.
67|
68|        === "File"
69|            A `charset` field may also be set to instruct which encoding to
70|            use for reading the file, defaulting to `utf-8`.
71|
72|            ```toml
73|            [project]
74|            ...
75|            readme = {"file" = "README.md", "content-type" = "text/markdown"}
76|            ```
77|
78|        === "Text"
79|            The `content-type` field must be set to `text/markdown` or `text/x-rst`.
80|
81|            ```toml
82|            [project]
83|            ...
84|            readme = {"text" = "...", "content-type" = "text/markdown"}
85|            ```
86|
87|!!! note
88|    If this is defined as a file, then it will always be included in [source distributions](../plugins/builder/sdist.md) for consistent builds.
89|
90|## Python support
91|
92|The Python version requirements of the project.
93|
94|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
95|[project]
96|...
97|requires-python = ">=3.8"
98|```
99|
100|## License
101|
102|For more information, see [PEP 639][].
103|
104|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: pyproject.toml"
105|
106|    === "SPDX expression"
107|
108|        ```toml
109|        [project]
110|        ...
111|        license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"
112|        ```
113|
114|    === "Files"
115|
116|        ```toml
117|        [project]
118|        ...
119|        license-files = ["LICENSES/*"]
120|        ```
121|
122|## Ownership
123|
124|The people or organizations considered to be the `authors` or `maintainers` of the project.
125|The exact meaning is open to interpretation; it may list the original or primary authors,
126|current maintainers, or owners of the package. If the values are the same, prefer only the
127|use of the `authors` field.
128|
129|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
130|[project]
131|...
132|authors = [
133|  { name = "...", email = "..." },
134|]
135|maintainers = [
136|  { name = "...", email = "..." },
137|]
138|```
139|
140|## Keywords
141|
142|The keywords used to assist in the discovery of the project.
143|
144|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
145|[project]
146|...
147|keywords = [
148|  "...",
149|]
150|```
151|
152|## Classifiers
153|
154|The [trove classifiers](https://pypi.org/classifiers/) that apply to the project.
155|
156|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
157|[project]
158|...
159|classifiers = [
160|  "...",
161|]
162|```
163|
164|## URLs
165|
166|A table of URLs where the key is the URL label and the value is the URL itself.
167|
168|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
169|[project.urls]
170|Documentation = "..."
171|"Source code" = "..."
172|```
173|
174|## Dependencies
175|
176|See the [dependency specification](dependency.md) page for more information.
177|
178|Entries support [context formatting](context.md) and [disallow direct references](#allowing-direct-references) by default.
179|
180|### Required
181|
182|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
183|[project]
184|...
185|dependencies = [
186|  "...",
187|]
188|```
189|
190|### Optional
191|
192|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
193|[project.optional-dependencies]
194|option1 = [
195|  "...",
196|]
197|option2 = [
198|  "...",
199|]
200|```
201|
202|## Entry points
203|
204|[Entry points](https://packaging.python.org/specifications/entry-points/) are a mechanism for
205|the project to advertise components it provides to be discovered and used by other code.
206|
207|### CLI
208|
209|After installing projects that define CLI scripts, each key will be available along your `PATH` as a command that will call its associated object.
210|
211|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
212|[project.scripts]
213|cli-name = "pkg.subpkg:func"
214|```
215|
216|Using the above example, running `cli-name` would essentially execute the following Python script:
217|
218|```python
219|import sys
220|
221|from pkg.subpkg import func
222|
223|sys.exit(func())
224|```
225|
226|### GUI
227|
228|GUI scripts are exactly the same as CLI scripts except on Windows, where they are handled specially so that they can be started without a console.
229|
230|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
231|[project.gui-scripts]
232|gui-name = "pkg.subpkg:func"
233|```
234|
235|### Plugins
236|
237|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
238|[project.entry-points.plugin-namespace]
239|plugin-name1 = "pkg.subpkg1"
240|plugin-name2 = "pkg.subpkg2:func"
241|```
242|
243|## Dynamic
244|
245|If any metadata fields are set dynamically, like the [`version`](#version) may be, then they must be listed here.
246|
247|```toml tab="pyproject.toml"
248|[project]
249|...
250|dynamic = [
251|  "...",
252|]
253|```
254|
255|## Metadata options
256|
257|### Allowing direct references
258|
259|By default, [dependencies](#dependencies) are not allowed to define [direct references](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#direct-references). To disable this check, set `allow-direct-references` to `true`:
260|
261|```toml config-example
262|[tool.hatch.metadata]
263|allow-direct-references = true
264|```
265|
266|### Allowing ambiguous features
267|
268|By default, names of [optional dependencies](#optional) are normalized to prevent ambiguity. To disable this normalization, set `allow-ambiguous-features` to `true`:
269|
270|```toml config-example
271|[tool.hatch.metadata]
272|allow-ambiguous-features = true
273|```
274|
275|!!! danger "Deprecated"
276|    This option temporarily exists to provide better interoperability with tools that do not yet support [PEP 685](https://peps.python.org/pep-0685/) and will be removed in the first minor release after Jan 1, 2024.

1|from __future__ import annotations
2|
3|import json
4|import os
5|import platform
6|import sys
7|from functools import lru_cache
8|from typing import Any
9|
10|from hatch._version import __version__
11|
12|
13|def get_linehaul_data() -> dict[str, Any]:
14|    data: dict[str, Any] = {
15|        "installer": {"name": "hatch", "version": __version__},
16|        "python": platform.python_version(),
17|        "implementation": {
18|            "name": platform.python_implementation(),
19|            "version": _get_implementation_version(),
20|        },
21|        "system": {
22|            "name": platform.system(),
23|            "release": platform.release(),
24|        },
25|        "cpu": platform.machine(),
26|        "ci": _looks_like_ci() or None,
27|    }
28|
29|    if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
30|        distro_info = _get_linux_distro_info()
31|        if distro_info:
32|            data["distro"] = distro_info
33|    elif sys.platform == "darwin":
34|        mac_version = platform.mac_ver()[0]
35|        if mac_version:
36|            data["distro"] = {"name": "macOS", "version": mac_version}
37|
38|    openssl_version = _get_openssl_version()
39|    if openssl_version:
40|        data["openssl_version"] = openssl_version
41|
42|    return data
43|
44|
45|def _get_implementation_version() -> str:
46|    implementation_name = platform.python_implementation()
47|
48|    if implementation_name == "PyPy":
49|        pypy_version_info = sys.pypy_version_info  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
50|        if pypy_version_info.releaselevel == "final":
51|            pypy_version_info = pypy_version_info[:3]
52|        return ".".join(str(x) for x in pypy_version_info)
53|
54|    return platform.python_version()
55|
56|
57|def _get_linux_distro_info() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
58|    import distro
59|
60|    name = distro.name()
61|    if not name:
62|        return None
63|
64|    distro_info: dict[str, Any] = {"name": name}
65|
66|    version = distro.version()
67|    if version:
68|        distro_info["version"] = version
69|
70|    codename = distro.codename()
71|    if codename:
72|        distro_info["id"] = codename
73|
74|    libc_info = _get_libc_info()
75|    if libc_info:
76|        distro_info["libc"] = libc_info
77|
78|    return distro_info
79|
80|
81|def _get_libc_info() -> dict[str, str] | None:
82|    libc, version = _get_libc_version()
83|    if libc and version:
84|        return {"lib": libc, "version": version}
85|    return None
86|
87|
88|def _get_libc_version() -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
89|    import ctypes
90|    import ctypes.util
91|
92|    libc_name = ctypes.util.find_library("c")
93|    if not libc_name:
94|        return None, None
95|
96|    try:
97|        libc = ctypes.CDLL(libc_name)
98|        libc.gnu_get_libc_version.restype = ctypes.c_char_p
99|        version = libc.gnu_get_libc_version()
100|        if version:
101|            return "glibc", version.decode()
102|    except (OSError, AttributeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
103|        pass
104|
105|    return None, None
106|
107|
108|def _get_openssl_version() -> str | None:
109|    try:
110|        import ssl
111|    except (ImportError, AttributeError):
112|        return None
113|    else:
114|        return ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION
115|
116|
117|def _looks_like_ci() -> bool:
118|    # INFO: Matches pip's CI detection for linehaul statistics.
119|    # Uses existence check (not value check) because variables like BUILD_BUILDID
120|    # and BUILD_ID are set to build IDs, not boolean strings.
121|    ci_env_vars = (
122|        "BUILD_BUILDID",
123|        "BUILD_ID",
124|        "CI",
125|        "GITHUB_ACTIONS",
126|        "GITLAB_CI",
127|        "PIP_IS_CI",
128|        "TRAVIS",
129|    )
130|    return any(env_var in os.environ for env_var in ci_env_vars)
131|
132|
133|@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
134|def get_linehaul_component() -> str:
135|    data = get_linehaul_data()
136|    return json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)

1|# Static analysis configuration
2|
3|-----
4|
5|Static analysis performed by the [`check code`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-code) and [`check fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-fmt) commands is ([by default](#customize-behavior)) backed entirely by [Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff).
6|
7|Hatch provides [default settings](#default-settings) that user configuration can [extend](#extending-config).
8|
9|!!! note
10|    The [`fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-fmt) command is being deprecated. Use `hatch check code` for linting and `hatch check fmt` for formatting instead.
11|
12|## Extending config
13|
14|When defining your configuration, be sure to use options that are prefixed by `extend-` such as [`extend-select`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#extend-select), for example:
15|
16|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: pyproject.toml"
17|
18|    ```toml
19|    [tool.ruff.format]
20|    preview = true
21|    quote-style = "single"
22|
23|    [tool.ruff.lint]
24|    preview = true
25|    extend-select = ["C901"]
26|
27|    [tool.ruff.lint.extend-per-file-ignores]
28|    "docs/.hooks/*" = ["INP001", "T201"]
29|
30|    [tool.ruff.lint.isort]
31|    known-first-party = ["foo", "bar"]
32|    ```
33|
34|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: ruff.toml"
35|
36|    ```toml
37|    [format]
38|    preview = true
39|    quote-style = "single"
40|
41|    [lint]
42|    preview = true
43|    extend-select = ["C901"]
44|
45|    [lint.extend-per-file-ignores]
46|    "docs/.hooks/*" = ["INP001", "T201"]
47|
48|    [lint.isort]
49|    known-first-party = ["foo", "bar"]
50|    ```
51|
52|!!! note
53|    When not [persisting config](#persistent-config), there is no need to explicitly [extend](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#extend) the defaults as Hatch automatically handles that.
54|
55|## Persistent config
56|
57|If you want to store the default configuration in the project, set an explicit path like so:
58|
59|```toml config-example
60|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-static-analysis]
61|config-path = "ruff_defaults.toml"
62|```
63|
64|Then instruct Ruff to consider your configuration as an extension of the default file:
65|
66|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: pyproject.toml"
67|
68|    ```toml
69|    [tool.ruff]
70|    extend = "ruff_defaults.toml"
71|    ```
72|
73|=== ":octicons-file-code-16: ruff.toml"
74|
75|    ```toml
76|    extend = "ruff_defaults.toml"
77|    ```
78|
79|Anytime you wish to update the defaults (such as when upgrading Hatch), you must run the [`check code`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-code) or [`check fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-fmt) command once with the `--sync` flag e.g.:
80|
81|```
82|hatch check code --sync
83|```
84|
85|!!! tip
86|    This is the recommended approach since it allows other tools like IDEs to use the default configuration.
87|
88|### No config
89|
90|If you don't want Hatch to use any of its default configuration and rely entirely on yours, set the path to anything and then simply don't `extend` in your Ruff config:
91|
92|```toml config-example
93|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-static-analysis]
94|config-path = "none"
95|```
96|
97|## Customize behavior
98|
99|You can fully alter the behavior of the environments used by the [`check code`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-code) and [`check fmt`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-check-fmt) commands. See the [how-to](../../how-to/static-analysis/behavior.md) for a detailed example.
100|
101|The `check code` command uses the `hatch-check-code` environment, and the `check fmt` command uses the `hatch-check-fmt` environment. The legacy `fmt` command continues to use the `hatch-static-analysis` environment.
102|
103|### Dependencies
104|
105|Pin the particular version of Ruff by explicitly defining the environment [dependencies](../environment/overview.md#dependencies):
106|
107|```toml config-example
108|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-code]
109|dependencies = ["ruff==X.Y.Z"]
110|
111|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-fmt]
112|dependencies = ["ruff==X.Y.Z"]
113|```
114|
115|### Scripts
116|
117|If you want to change the default commands that are executed, you can override the [scripts](../environment/overview.md#scripts).
118|
119|For the `hatch-check-code` environment:
120|
121|```toml config-example
122|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-code.scripts]
123|lint-check = "..."
124|lint-fix = "..."
125|```
126|
127|For the `hatch-check-fmt` environment:
128|
129|```toml config-example
130|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-fmt.scripts]
131|format-check = "..."
132|format-fix = "..."
133|```
134|
135|The `*-fix` scripts run by default while the `*-check` scripts run when the `--fix` flag is not passed.
136|
137|!!! note "Reminder"
138|    If you choose to use different tools for static analysis, be sure to update the required [dependencies](#dependencies).
139|
140|### Installer
141|
142|By default, [UV is enabled](../../how-to/environment/select-installer.md). You may disable that behavior as follows:
143|
144|```toml config-example
145|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-code]
146|installer = "pip"
147|
148|[tool.hatch.envs.hatch-check-fmt]
149|installer = "pip"
150|```

19|def get_wheel_form_data(artifact):
20|    import zipfile
21|
22|    from packaging.tags import parse_tag
23|
24|    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(artifact), "r") as zip_archive:
25|        for path in zip_archive.namelist():
26|            root = path.split("/", 1)[0]
27|            if root.endswith(".dist-info"):
28|                dist_info_dir = root
29|                break
30|        else:  # no cov
31|            message = f"Could not find the `.dist-info` directory in wheel: {artifact}"
32|            raise ArtifactMetadataError(message)
33|
34|        try:
35|            with zip_archive.open(f"{dist_info_dir}/METADATA") as zip_file:
36|                metadata_file_contents = zip_file.read().decode("utf-8")
37|        except KeyError:  # no cov
38|            message = f"Could not find a `METADATA` file in the `{dist_info_dir}` directory"
39|            raise ArtifactMetadataError(message) from None
40|        else:
41|            data = parse_headers(metadata_file_contents)
42|
43|    data["filetype"] = "bdist_wheel"
44|
45|    # Examples:
46|    # cryptography-3.4.7-pp37-pypy37_pp73-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl -> pp37
47|    # hatchling-1rc1-py2.py3-none-any.whl -> py2.py3
48|    tag_component = "-".join(artifact.stem.split("-")[-3:])
49|    data["pyversion"] = ".".join(sorted({tag.interpreter for tag in parse_tag(tag_component)}))
50|
51|    return data

54|def get_sdist_form_data(artifact):
55|    import tarfile
56|
57|    with tarfile.open(str(artifact), "r:gz") as tar_archive:
58|        pkg_info_dir_parts = []
59|        for tar_info in tar_archive:
60|            if tar_info.isfile():
61|                pkg_info_dir_parts.append(tar_info.name.split("/", 1)[0])
62|                break
63|        else:  # no cov
64|            message = f"Could not find any files in sdist: {artifact}"
65|            raise ArtifactMetadataError(message)
66|
67|        pkg_info_dir_parts.append("PKG-INFO")
68|        pkg_info_path = "/".join(pkg_info_dir_parts)
69|        try:
70|            with tar_archive.extractfile(pkg_info_path) as tar_file:
71|                metadata_file_contents = tar_file.read().decode("utf-8")
72|        except KeyError:  # no cov
73|            message = f"Could not find file: {pkg_info_path}"
74|            raise ArtifactMetadataError(message) from None
75|        else:
76|            data = parse_headers(metadata_file_contents)
77|
78|    data["filetype"] = "sdist"
79|    data["pyversion"] = "source"
80|
81|    return data
82|
83|
84|def parse_headers(metadata_file_contents):
85|    import email
86|
87|    message = email.message_from_string(metadata_file_contents)
88|
89|    headers = {"description": message.get_payload()}
90|
91|    for header, value in message.items():
92|        normalized_header = header.lower().replace("-", "_")
93|        header_name = RENAMED_METADATA_FIELDS.get(normalized_header, normalized_header)
94|
95|        if normalized_header in MULTIPLE_USE_METADATA_FIELDS:
96|            if header_name in headers:
97|                headers[header_name].append(value)
98|            else:
99|                headers[header_name] = [value]
100|        else:
101|            headers[header_name] = value
102|
103|    return headers

1|# FAQ

3|-----
4|
5|## Interoperability
6|
7|***Q***: What is the risk of lock-in?
8|
9|***A***: Not much! Other than the [plugin system](../plugins/about.md), everything uses Python's established standards by default. Project metadata is based entirely on [the standard][project metadata standard], the build system is compatible with [PEP 517][]/[PEP 660][], versioning uses the scheme specified by [PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#public-version-identifiers), dependencies are defined with [PEP 508][] strings, and environments use [virtualenv](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv).
10|
11|***Q***: Must one use all features?
12|
13|***A***: No, all features are optional! You can use [just the build system](../build.md#packaging-ecosystem), publish wheels and source distributions that were built by other tools, only use the environment management, etc.
14|
15|## Libraries vs applications
16|
17|***Q***: Are workflows for both libraries and applications supported?
18|
19|***A***: Yes, mostly! Applications can utilize environment management just like libraries, and plugins can be used to [build](../plugins/builder/reference.md) projects in arbitrary formats or [publish](../plugins/publisher/reference.md) artifacts to arbitrary destinations.
20|
21|The only caveat is that currently there is no support for re-creating an environment given a set of dependencies in a reproducible manner. Although a standard lock file format may be far off since [PEP 665][] was rejected, resolving capabilities are [coming to pip](https://github.com/pypa/pip/pull/10748). When that is stabilized, Hatch will add locking functionality and dedicated documentation for managing applications.
22|

202|## Fast CLI?
203|
204|The claim about being faster than other tools is [based on timings](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/actions/workflows/cli.yml) that are always checked in CI.
205|
206|Hatch achieves this by using lazy imports, lazily performing computation manually and with [functools.cached_property](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functools.html#functools.cached_property), using hacks like `not not ...` instead of `bool(...)`, etc.

1|from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
2|
3|from hatch.env.utils import get_verbosity_flag
4|from hatchling.utils.context import ContextFormatter
5|
6|
7|class EnvironmentContextFormatterBase(ContextFormatter, ABC):
8|    @abstractmethod
9|    def formatters(self):
10|        return {}
11|
12|
13|class EnvironmentContextFormatter(EnvironmentContextFormatterBase):
14|    def __init__(self, environment):
15|        self.environment = environment
16|        self.CONTEXT_NAME = f"environment_{environment.PLUGIN_NAME}"
17|
18|    def formatters(self):  # noqa: PLR6301
19|        """
20|        This returns a mapping of supported field names to their respective formatting functions. Each function
21|        accepts 2 arguments:
22|
23|        - the `value` that was passed to the format call, defaulting to `None`
24|        - the modifier `data`, defaulting to an empty string
25|        """
26|        return {}
27|
28|    def get_formatters(self):
29|        formatters = {
30|            "args": self.__format_args,
31|            "env_name": self.__format_env_name,
32|            "env_type": self.__format_env_type,
33|            "matrix": self.__format_matrix,
34|            "verbosity": self.__format_verbosity,
35|        }
36|        formatters.update(self.formatters())
37|        return formatters
38|
39|    def __format_args(self, value, data):  # noqa: PLR6301
40|        if value is not None:
41|            return value
42|
43|        return data or ""
44|
45|    def __format_env_name(self, value, data):  # noqa: ARG002
46|        return self.environment.name
47|
48|    def __format_env_type(self, value, data):  # noqa: ARG002
49|        return self.environment.PLUGIN_NAME
50|
51|    def __format_matrix(self, value, data):  # noqa: ARG002
52|        if not data:
53|            message = "The `matrix` context formatting field requires a modifier"
54|            raise ValueError(message)
55|
56|        variable, separator, default = data.partition(":")
57|        if variable in self.environment.matrix_variables:
58|            return self.environment.matrix_variables[variable]
59|
60|        if not separator:
61|            message = f"Nonexistent matrix variable must set a default: {variable}"
62|            raise ValueError(message)
63|
64|        return default
65|
66|    def __format_verbosity(self, value, data):  # noqa: ARG002
67|        if not data:
68|            return str(self.environment.verbosity)
69|
70|        modifier, _, adjustment = data.partition(":")
71|        if modifier != "flag":
72|            message = f"Unknown verbosity modifier: {modifier}"
73|            raise ValueError(message)
74|
75|        if not adjustment:
76|            adjustment = "0"
77|
78|        try:
79|            adjustment = int(adjustment)
80|        except ValueError:
81|            message = f"Verbosity flag adjustment must be an integer: {adjustment}"
82|            raise TypeError(message) from None
83|
84|        return get_verbosity_flag(self.environment.verbosity, adjustment=adjustment)

1|# How to use lockfiles
2|
3|-----
4|
5|Hatch can generate [PEP 751](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/) lockfiles (`pylock.toml`) for your environments. Lockfiles capture the exact resolved versions and hashes of all dependencies, ensuring reproducible installations across machines and CI.
6|
7|## Configuring locked environments
8|
9|To use lockfiles, first configure which environments should be locked by setting [`locked = true`](../../config/environment/overview.md#locked):
10|
11|```toml config-example
12|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
13|locked = true
14|dependencies = [
15|  "pytest",
16|]
17|```
18|
19|Or enable it globally for all environments with the [`lock-envs`](../../config/environment/overview.md#lock-envs) setting:
20|
21|```toml config-example
22|[tool.hatch]
23|lock-envs = true
24|```
25|
26|Individual environments can opt out:
27|
28|```toml config-example
29|[tool.hatch]
30|lock-envs = true
31|
32|[tool.hatch.envs.docs]
33|locked = false
34|```
35|
36|## Generating lockfiles
37|
38|### `hatch env lock` (all or named environments)
39|
40|Use the [`env lock`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-env-lock) command to generate lockfiles. When called without arguments, it locks all environments configured with `locked = true`:
41|
42|```console
43|$ hatch env lock
44|Locking environment: default
45|Wrote lockfile: /path/to/project/pylock.toml
46|Locking environment: test
47|Wrote lockfile: /path/to/project/pylock.test.toml
48|```
49|
50|You can also lock a specific environment by name:
51|
52|```console
53|$ hatch env lock test
54|Locking environment: test
55|Wrote lockfile: /path/to/project/pylock.test.toml
56|```
57|
58|!!! note
59|    When locking a specific environment by name, it must have `locked = true` configured. To generate a lockfile for an environment that is not configured as locked, use the `--export` flag.
60|
61|The `default` environment produces `pylock.toml`, while all other environments produce `pylock.<ENV_NAME>.toml`, following the [PEP 751](https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/) naming convention.
62|
63|### `hatch dep lock` and `hatch lock` (active environment)
64|
65|For the environment selected with `-e` / `HATCH_ENV` (see the [CLI](../../cli/about.md)), you can run:
66|
67|- [`dep lock`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-lock) — same resolver options as `env lock` where applicable (`--upgrade`, `--upgrade-package`, `--export`, `--export-all`, `--check`).
68|- [`lock`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-lock) — shorthand for `hatch dep lock`.
69|
70|Matrix parents and other names still expand the same way as elsewhere; `--export-all` locks every configured environment into a directory, matching `hatch env lock --export-all`.
71|
72|## Syncing from a lockfile
73|
74|[`dep sync`](../../cli/reference.md#hatch-dep-sync) runs the selected locker’s **`apply_lock`** step for the active environment (for example `uv pip sync` when using the UV locker). The environment must be [`locked`](../../config/environment/overview.md#locked) and the lockfile must already exist—run `hatch dep lock` or `hatch env lock` first.
75|
76|## Automatic locking
77|
78|Environments with `locked = true` will have their lockfiles generated automatically during `hatch env create` or `hatch run` whenever:
79|
80|- The lockfile does not exist yet
81|- The environment's dependencies have changed
82|
83|## Updating locked dependencies
84|
85|To upgrade all locked packages to their latest allowed versions:
86|
87|```console
88|$ hatch env lock test --upgrade
89|```
90|
91|To upgrade only specific packages:
92|
93|```console
94|$ hatch env lock test --upgrade-package requests --upgrade-package urllib3
95|```
96|
97|## Checking if a lockfile is up-to-date
98|
99|Use `--check` on `hatch env lock`, `hatch dep lock`, or `hatch lock` to verify the lockfile is **in sync** with the current dependency inputs (re-resolve and compare). If there is nothing to lock for that environment, Hatch only checks that the file exists.
100|
101|```console
102|$ hatch env lock test --check
103|Lockfile is up to date: /path/to/project/pylock.test.toml
104|```
105|
106|This is useful in CI to ensure lockfiles have been committed and match `pyproject.toml` / env dependencies.
107|
108|## Exporting lockfiles
109|
110|To generate a lockfile for an environment that is not configured with `locked = true`, or to write to a custom location, use `--export`:
111|
112|```console
113|$ hatch env lock default --export locks/default.lock
114|```
115|
116|To export lockfiles for all environments into a directory, use `--export-all`:
117|
118|```console
119|$ hatch env lock --export-all locks/
120|```
121|
122|!!! note
123|    `--export` and `--export-all` are mutually exclusive.
124|
125|## Custom lock filenames
126|
127|You can override the default filename for any environment with the [`lock-filename`](../../config/environment/overview.md#lock-filename) option:
128|
129|```toml config-example
130|[tool.hatch.envs.test]
131|lock-filename = "requirements-test.lock"
132|```
133|
134|When multiple matrix environments share the same `lock-filename`, Hatch will merge their dependencies and generate the lockfile once.
135|
136|## Installer integration and locker selection
137|
138|By default, Hatch picks a built-in **locker** from the environment installer:
139|
140|- **pip** (default): `pip lock` (requires pip 25.1+) for generation.
141|- **UV**: `uv pip compile` (with hashes) and `uv pip sync` when applying a lock.
142|
143|Override with [`tool.hatch.locker`](../../config/environment/overview.md#locker) or [`tool.hatch.envs.<name>.locker`](../../config/environment/overview.md#locker). See [Dependency locker plugins](../../plugins/locker.md) to implement `hatch_register_locker`.
144|
145|See [Dependency locker plugins](../../plugins/locker.md) for the full plugin interface.
